rows.why: US booked through FY29 with a INR5,500 crore data-centre pipeline order won recently, and management expects demand to last 3 to 5 years beyond FY29, though ordering intensity will slow.

rows.label: Saudi utilisation ramp to 50-60% in year one
rows.why: Management targets at least 50-60% utilisation in the first year, with a fast ramp if the supply chain stabilises, but order materialisation has been delayed by Middle East disruption.

rows.label: Saudi anti-dumping duty on DI pipe imports
rows.why: Management noted anti-dumping duty on DI pipe imports in Saudi Arabia, with about two-thirds of captive DI requirement served by imports, supporting Welspun's first right of refusal on local demand.

tone.note: Management was confident on US and Saudi medium-term demand, record financials and 22.7% ROCE, but cautious on near-term India domestic water demand, Middle East logistics and FY27 guidance; analysts pressed on US order intensity beyond FY29, Saudi utilisation and the use of the net cash pile.

532149|2026-06.headline: Bank of India Q1 FY27 net profit rose 36.23% YoY to Rs 3,068 crore; Global NIM eased to 2.52% and FY27 guidance was kept unchanged.
532149|2026-06.overview: Bank of India reported Q1 FY27 net profit of Rs 3,068 crore, up 36.23% YoY, with operating profit up 25.99% to Rs 5,051 crore and NII up 12.61% to Rs 6,833 crore. Asset quality improved on a YoY basis, with Gross NPA at 1.81% and Net NPA at 0.51%, and slippage ratio at 0.24%. Global business grew 16.57% YoY to Rs 17.55 lakh crore, with advances up 18.64%. Management reiterated FY27 guidance for advances growth of 15-16% and deposit growth of 13-14%, and raised a dollar-funding target of $4.2 billion through FCNR(B), OFCB/MTN and ECB routes by December 2026.

financial_highlights.change: GNPA -111 bps YoY; NNPA -24 bps YoY

segments.name: Global business and deposits
segments.commentary: Global business Rs 17.55 lakh crore (+16.57% YoY). Global deposits Rs 9.58 lakh crore (+14.90%); domestic deposits Rs 8.25 lakh crore (+16.15%). CASA Rs 3.02 lakh crore, CASA ratio 36.68%.

segments.name: Advances
segments.commentary: Global gross advances Rs 7.98 lakh crore (+18.64% YoY); domestic advances Rs 6.74 lakh crore (+19.20%). RAM advances Rs 3.93 lakh crore (+19.75%), 58.30% of advances.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book about Rs 57,000 crore at yield of about 9.10%, growing about 52% YoY; NPA below Rs 100 crore.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: International business touched about Rs 2.56 lakh crore; around 32% of international loan book is trade finance, which management plans to reduce.

segments.name: Mutual fund subsidiary
segments.commentary: Bank of India mutual fund AUM about Rs 16,000-17,000 crore; no near-term plan for public issue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 global advances growth guidance unchanged at 15-16%; global deposit growth guidance unchanged at 13-14%.
Global NIM guidance for FY27 at 2.55%-2.60%, though management said NIMs are under challenge.
Cost-to-income ratio at about 46% in Q1, but guided to 48%-49% on a consistent basis during FY27.
ROA guidance of 1% and above on a consistent quarter-on-quarter basis in FY27 (Q4 FY26 1.01%, Q1 FY27 about 1%).
FCNR(B) target of $1.2 billion by 30 September 2026; OFCB/MTN target about $2 billion by 31 December 2026; ECB target about $1 billion; total dollar raising about $4.2 billion by December 2026.
capex_capacity: Opened a dedicated Strategic Business Branch in Mumbai for high-value pool buyouts, co-lending, TReDS and supply chain financing.
Centralised Video KYC centre operationalised in Mumbai for end-to-end digital account opening.
Around 22% of domestic credit book now sanctioned digitally; data lake and CRM Next linked lead flow has built business of more than Rs 18,000 crore.
ATM network rationalised: loss-making capex-model ATMs exited, reducing total ATM count by about 300.
Plans to add 19 emerging corporate credit branches' focus on Rs 25-250 crore mid-corporate advances; credit card base target of 3 lakh by end FY27.
demand_pricing: Corporate plus international pipeline about Rs 70,000 crore; total loan pipeline above Rs 1 lakh crore including RAM, digital, pool purchase, TReDS and supply chain financing.

FCNR(B) deposits: about $200 million garnered so far; three-year FCNR at 6.25%, 3-4 year at 6.30%, five-year at 6.50%; leverage product up to nine times; management cited a spread of about 50 bps on five-year deposits, with CRR/SLR not applicable.
Management declined to give current leverage spread, citing a moving target in borrowing and dollar rates; leveraged share of FCNR not quantified.
Personal loans grew only about 3% YoY after guardrails were put on low-ticket and non-salaried personal loans.
ECLGS: about Rs 6,000 crore sanctioned, Rs 4,600 crore disbursed; expected total sanctions and disbursal of about Rs 8,000 crore by scheme end.
SMA-0 for accounts of Rs 5 crore and above fell to about Rs 4,090 crore (0.52% of standard book), from about Rs 4,700 crore at March 2026 and above Rs 7,000 crore at June 2025.
Q1 fresh slippages including incremental NPA debits about Rs 1,800 crore vs Rs 2,100 crore in Q1 FY26; sectors under watch include chemicals, ceramics and oil/gas importers/exporters.
PSL income about Rs 277 crore in Q1; management said further PSL income possible in Q2 and Q3 but gave no number.

qa_highlights.question: Is stress visible in MSME and small loan accounts from the West Asia crisis, and what is the ECLGS position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SMA and slippages show no major stress; ECLGS sanctions of about Rs 6,000 crore with Rs 4,600 crore disbursed, expected to reach about Rs 8,000 crore. Certain sectors are being monitored closely.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FCNR, OFCB/MTN and ECB plan and how does the leverage product work?
qa_highlights.answer: FCNR(B) target is $1.2 billion by 30 September; OFCB/MTN about $2 billion by 31 December; ECB about $1 billion (about $500 million already approved in principle). Leverage product is up to nine times, with three-year FCNR at 6.25%.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan strategy and growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold loan book about Rs 57,000 crore at about 9.10% yield, growing about 52% YoY; NPA below Rs 100 crore; three-notice, 90-day auction SOP applied.

qa_highlights.question: Why did personal loans grow only 3%, and what is the credit card plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Guardrails were put on low-ticket and non-salaried personal loans, shifting to salaried and service-sector borrowers with NACH. Credit card base target is 3 lakh by end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CASA and retail term deposit ratios fall while cost of deposits dropped 15 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a roughly 3% fall in CASA and retail term deposit share, as bulk deposits above Rs 3 crore were used to fund credit growth; cost of deposits was reduced via Rs 3-25 crore FD campaign and mix changes.

qa_highlights.question: Will NIM and CIR hold, and how will yields on advances move?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is NIM 2.55%-2.60% and CIR 48%-49% for FY27. Yields on advances expected to pause falling, supported by MCLR-linked loans, mid-corporate growth and reduced low-margin trade finance.

risks_watch: Dollar-raising targets ($4.2 billion) depend on FCNR, OFCB/MTN and ECB windows (FCNR to 30 September; OFCB/MTN to 31 December 2026); leverage spreads are moving.
NIM under pressure from the interest rate environment and West Asia developments; guidance requires 2.55%-2.60% vs 2.52% in Q1.
CIR guidance steps up to 48%-49% from about 46% in Q1, implying higher costs ahead.
Stress in chemicals, ceramics and oil/gas-linked import/export accounts; Q1 is seasonally high for slippages per management.
Declining CASA ratio (36.68%) and retail term deposits; cost of deposits benefit depends on bulk and FCNR mix.
Treasury gains in Q1 may not repeat as yields move adversely.
532149|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on headline growth, asset quality and profitability, with guidance reiterated unchanged. Cautious on NIM, the West Asia impact and sector stress, and evasive on FCNR spreads and leverage economics and on the PSU merger question.
key_quotes: But our guidance for the global NIM is somewhere around 2.55 % to 2.60% for FY27.
So , we are very confident that Quite a few.
Yes, $1.2 billion is our target that we have set for ourselves that and we are very confident that we'll be achieving it very quickly.

rows.why: Global advances up 18.64% YoY to Rs 7.98 lakh crore and FY27 guidance held at 15-16%, backed by a Rs 1 lakh crore+ loan pipeline including Rs 70,000 crore corporate and international.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: FCNR(B) leverage product (up to nine times) and FCNR rates of 6.25%-6.50% are already live, and a Mumbai Strategic Business Branch has opened, but no new product launch date was given.

rows.label: Rs 1 lakh crore+ loan pipeline
rows.why: Total pipeline above Rs 1 lakh crore, including Rs 70,000 crore corporate and international, backs FY27 advances growth guidance of 15-16%.

rows.label: Dollar raise of $4.2 billion by December 2026
rows.why: FCNR(B) target $1.2 billion by 30 September, OFCB/MTN about $2 billion and ECB about $1 billion; only about $200 million of FCNR garnered so far.

rows.label: ECLGS disbursal to about Rs 8,000 crore
rows.why: About Rs 6,000 crore sanctioned and Rs 4,600 crore disbursed so far, with total expected at about Rs 8,000 crore.

tone.note: Management was confident on advances growth, asset quality (GNPA 1.81%, SMA-0 down to Rs 4,090 crore) and ROA about 1%, but cautious on NIM (2.52%), the West Asia impact and sector stress, and evasive on FCNR leverage spreads and the PSU merger question.

532149|2026-09.headline: Bank of India Q2 FY27: H1 net profit about Rs 6,000 crore, Global NIM 2.47%, Gross NPA 1.60%; ECL front-loading planned from Q3, about 0.5% CRAR impact per year.
532149|2026-09.overview: Management reported strong YoY growth: global business up 21.13% to Rs 18.92 lakh crore, and global advances up 20.58%. Operating profit rose 33.18% to Rs 5,089 crore and net profit rose 25.32% to Rs 3,202 crore for Sept'26 (the Q2 figure as stated on the call). Asset quality improved, with Gross NPA at 1.60% and Net NPA at 0.42%, and credit cost fell to 0.12% from 0.15% in June'26. 532156|2026-03.headline: Vaibhav Global FY26: PBT up 41% YoY, record FCF of INR272 crore, EBITDA margin 10.8%; FY27 guidance 9-11% revenue growth and 50-100 bps margin expansion.
532156|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR935 crore (+10% YoY) with EBITDA of INR96 crore (about 10.3%) and PBT of INR64 crore (+41% YoY). segments.commentary: Revenue INR70.9 crores, +32.4% YoY, described as another strong quarter.

segments.name: Digital (B2C)
segments.commentary: Digital revenue INR367 crores, +5.6% YoY in rupee terms and marginally down YoY due to Shopify migration; digital share of B2C revenue fell about 3 percentage points versus Q1, and 44% of U.S. revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 7-9%, cut from 9-11%, citing the Shopify transition, U.K. warehouse consolidation, weaker U.K. consumer and U.S. midterm election risk.
FY27 EBITDA margin now expected broadly in line with FY26, versus earlier guidance of 50-100 bps expansion.
Management remains confident of returning to 9-11% revenue growth in FY28.
Digital share target of 50% of B2C revenue by Q4 FY27 retained, with digital expected to return to its earlier growth trajectory post-transition.
Sustainable effective tax rate of 18-20% over the next 2-3 years, with German losses set off in coming periods and absorption extending beyond FY28.
Target of INR5,000-5,500 crores by FY30 excludes any new country launch such as India; mostly organic with possible small digital acquisition.
Second interim dividend of INR1.5 per share declared, following INR1.5 in Q1 FY27.
capex_capacity: Capex of about INR63 crores cited in Q2 call, of which about INR36 crores relates to U.K. warehouse consolidation into a single premises; the rest is tech improvement and Shopify migration.
Inventory build of roughly INR100 crores year-on-year for festive readiness; inventory days expected to moderate to the 200-220 day range by Q3 and Q4.
U.K. warehouse consolidation still in progress per management, with all stock moved into one warehouse.
Germany to reach robust profitability before any new country entry; India launch 'on the cards' but not in the FY30 target.
demand_pricing: Retail volumes grew about 2% overall, driven by lower price point items; consumers seeking value.
Gross margin expansion attributed to vertical integration, in-house brands and lab-grown diamond (LGD) mix; management says it can hold around 64-65% gross margin despite precious metal price moves.
LGD share rose to 12% of total retail revenue from about 10% a year earlier; in-house brands 57% of B2C revenue; lifestyle about 40% of B2C; budget about 35% of retail revenue.
Customer metrics (trailing 12 months): 127 million households reached, 687,000 unique customers, 360,000 new customers, 38% retention, 23 pieces bought per customer per year.
Management cited peer growth (revolve.com double-digit) to argue digital growth of 17-20% is achievable; current digital growth has been below 20% in constant currency for 2-3 years per analyst.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify revenue lost from the Shopify migration.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about USD2.8 million, or roughly 2.8% of growth, in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why is capex around INR63 crores and what is it for?
qa_highlights.answer: Nitin Panwad said about INR36 crores is for U.K. warehouse consolidation into one premises; the rest is tech improvement and Shopify migration.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory build of roughly INR100 crores year-on-year for festive season readiness and global uncertainty; inventory days expected to return to 200-220 by Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company buy back shares given ongoing dividends?
qa_highlights.answer: The Board kept the dividend tradition; management said it wants to build cash for acquisitions or strategic moves and will deploy surplus cash into a buyback afterwards.

qa_highlights.question: Why was U.K. so much weaker than U.S. and Germany?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited two disruptions (Shopify and warehouse consolidation) plus a weaker U.K. economy and cost-of-living pressure, while Germany is a newer business with a larger customer base.

qa_highlights.question: How will digital reach the growth required for 9-11%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to faster product testing, AI-personalised creatives and six brands on the new platform, and said the numbers were modelled in detail; it did not give a specific digital growth figure.

risks_watch: Shopify stabilisation and customer acquisition cost: management targets payback within 6 months but says it is not yet at the 3-month goal.
U.K. consumer weakness and consolidation execution; U.K. revenue fell 7% in constant currency.
Digital growth must re-accelerate sharply (management did not quantify; analyst estimated 17-20%+) to meet FY28 9-11% target.
Inventory of about INR100 crores higher year-on-year and net cash down to INR186 crores from INR279 crores.
Shareholder pressure for buybacks versus continued dividends; stock price weakness raised by an individual shareholder.
U.S. midterm election potentially diverting TV viewership; TV home attrition noted.

Answers on buybacks and India expansion were deferential and non-committal, and detail on digital growth targets was thin.
key_quotes: Q2 was a quarter of transition and an important one.
We see these pressures as transitional.
We believe this is the right call, and it does not change our medium-term view.
Shopify is a strategic step towards achieving this objective, positioning us to accelerate digital growth and drive sustainable profitable growth over the medium term.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Six brands moved to the new platform and faster product testing with AI-personalised creatives was cited, but no specific product or brand launch date was given; LGD mix rose to 12% of retail revenue.

rows.label: Inventory days back to 200-220 by Q3-Q4
rows.why: Inventory build of about INR100 crores YoY for festive readiness, with management guiding inventory days to moderate to 200-220 by Q3 and Q4; net cash already fell to INR186 crores from INR279 crores.

rows.label: Buyback after cash build for acquisitions
rows.why: Management said it wants to build cash for acquisitions or strategic moves and would deploy surplus into a buyback afterwards, with net cash at INR186 crores; no date or size given.

rows.label: Digital share 50% of B2C by Q4 FY27

tone.note: Management was confident on the FY28 9-11% recovery and digital share target but openly cut FY27 guidance and called the Q2 hit transitional; analysts pressed on digital growth figures, U.K. weakness and buybacks, and management gave thin, deferential answers on those.

532163|2026-03.headline: Saregama Q4 FY26 revenue rose 19% YoY to INR 287 crore and adjusted EBITDA hit a record INR 133 crore (+31% YoY).
532163|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 287 crore (+19% YoY), with adjusted EBITDA of INR 133 crore (+31% YoY) and operational PBT of INR 105 crore (+37% YoY). Management attributed the Q4 acceleration partly to the exit of Airtel Wynk, which shut in November 2024 and is no longer in the base. Music vertical (licensing, artiste management and retail combined) grew 17% in FY26 to INR 814 crore, with H1 at +8% and H2 at +26%. New content spend was INR 235 crore, below plan, as large films such as Love & War and Paradise slipped into FY27.

financial_highlights.change: Lower YoY; FY25 included Diljit Dosanjh tour
Below plan; plus INR 105 crore on inorganic catalogue purchases
Management cited FY26 net of other income at INR 73 crore vs INR 37 crore in FY25 (analyst cited INR 7 crore FY23, INR 16 crore FY24, INR 36 crore FY25)

segments.name: Music (licensing + artiste management + retail)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 814 crore (+17%), EBITDA INR 517 crore (+22%), net margin INR 377 crore (+28%). Medium-term guidance: 20-23% revenue CAGR and 60-65% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Video
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 108 crore (-44%), a conscious exit from in-house film production under Yoodlee in favour of the Bhansali Productions stake. Focus is now TV serials and short-format content; no major new projects greenlit.

segments.name: Live events
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 62 crore. Launched first festival IP UN40 (12,000 footfalls, 8 sponsors) with a loss; breakeven targeted FY28. Carvaan Live and US tours planned for FY27.

segments.name: Pocket Aces (digital)
segments.commentary: Reached breakeven in FY26 per management; Saregama owns 91%.

segments.name: Artiste management and brand partnerships
segments.commentary: Managed artists increased to 300+ (about 30 added in the quarter), with over 400 Mn followers. New brand partnerships vertical covers music, live events and short-format video.

guidance_outlook: Music vertical medium-term revenue CAGR of 20-23%; annual music EBITDA margin of 60-65%.
New content budget for FY27 of INR 300-350 crore; FY25-FY27 cumulative around INR 1,000 crore.
From FY28, content investment to rise linearly at high-single to low-double-digit YoY, not in step-jumps; target 25-30% market share of new content.
Music net margins expected to improve 300-500 bps over 3-5 years (management clarified EBIT margin around 46-50%).
UN40 festival to run annually (next edition February 2027); breakeven expected FY28. Video capital allocation to fall to mid-single digits of total capital deployed from around 18%.
Punjabi music push: results expected in 2-3 quarters, possibly by end-FY27 or Q3.
capex_capacity: New content spend FY26 INR 235 crore vs plan; FY27 slate includes Love & War, Naagzilla, Rajinikanth's next Tamil film, Seyon and Paradise.

Strategic minority investment in Bhansali Productions completed in Q4 FY26; valuation linked to its financial performance over three years, giving access to A and B+ Hindi film music for 24-30 months. Its share of profit will be booked via equity method.
Catalogue of about 180,000 songs, adding about 5,500 new releases per year.
Festival UN40 launched in Q4 FY26 as season 1; Carvaan Live small-concert series planned for FY27.
demand_pricing: Management says the industry grew 7-8% in FY26 per E&Y/FICCI and IMI; Saregama grew faster, aided by new content.
Platform shutdowns (Resso, Wynk, Hungama, Gaana going fully paid) distorted the denominator; management says this headwind is over.
Paid streaming penetration in India below 3% vs 57% in US; management cites 64% of free users willing to pay if free options stopped.
Short-format video licensing remains one-year fixed-fee deals; social media deals are flat fee.
Q4 financials are affected by timing: society payments come in Q4, and Dhurandhar marketing sat in Q3 with revenue in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Punjabi music weak, and how much will be allocated over the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management admitted two past failed attempts in six years. A combined recorded-plus-live deal model is planned, with results expected by end-FY27 or Q3; no allocation figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Were provision write-backs in revenue and do they explain the ~42% margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Write-backs relate to royalty provisions and sit in cost of revenue, not in revenue. Q1 provisions unwound in Q4; management asks for rolling 12-month evaluation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 content budget, and what was the impact of Airtel Wynk ending?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 new content budget is INR 300-350 crore. Wynk shut in November 2024; customers moved to Spotify, Saavn, Amazon, Gaana, Apple and YouTube.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the music margin step-up (net margin 42% FY25 to 47-48% FY26)?
qa_highlights.answer: Heavy content amortisation was booked in FY25 (Stree 2, Amaran); FY26 benefits from earlier content with lower charge-off.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the events business post a loss in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: The loss is mainly UN40, a year-one festival; festivals take 3-4 years to breakeven. Losses expected to shrink year-on-year, breakeven in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the unallocable expense increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to lower interest income on the QIP funds deployed into content and Bhansali, which reduces netting off against other income. A detailed reconciliation was deferred offline.

risks_watch: Revenue timing is lumpy: Love & War and Paradise slipped from Q4 to FY27, and management said quarterly swings are normal.
Content amortisation and marketing charge-offs can distort quarterly margins; management asks investors to use rolling 12-month figures.
UN40 and Carvaan Live losses in the events business, plus the Bhansali investment, are unproven for returns.
Unallocable expenses rose sharply (analyst cited INR 37 crore FY25 to INR 73 crore FY26); management deferred a full explanation offline.
ROE is 13.3%, which management said is not satisfactory; the stock has been in a downtrend for several quarters.
Unreconciled point on advances and cash position; the call also raised an IPRS dispute, which management said has no implication.

This decline is by design and has not happened by chance.
We are steadfast in maintaining that we will grow it, keeping in mind strong economic principles and never do things which are coming out of vanity.

rows.why: No utilisation data or new capacity plan was given; the capital deployed (QIP funds into content and Bhansali) is an investment in content and a minority stake rather than a capacity build, so a new capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.why: Music revenue grew 17% in FY26 with H2 at +26% against 20-23% medium-term CAGR guidance, and the FY27 content slate is named, so an upgrade is possible if H2 momentum holds.

rows.why: Revenue timing is lumpy: Love & War and Paradise slipped from Q4 FY26 into FY27, and FY26 new content spend of INR 235 crore came in below plan, so quarterly misses are possible even though the medium-term guide was held.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: FY27 (Carvaan Live Q2 FY27; UN40 next edition Feb 2027)
rows.why: Carvaan Live small-concert series is planned for FY27 and UN40 runs annually with next edition in February 2027; the Punjabi music combined model is expected by end-FY27 or Q3 with no allocation figure.

rows.label: Bhansali Productions access to A and B+ Hindi film music
rows.why: Strategic minority stake completed in Q4 FY26 gives access to A and B+ Hindi film music for 24-30 months, with share of profit booked via equity method.

rows.label: UN40 festival breakeven
rows.why: UN40 season 1 drew 12,000 footfalls and 8 sponsors with a loss; management expects losses to shrink YoY and breakeven by FY28.

rows.label: Unallocable expense normalisation
rows.why: Unallocable expense rose from INR 37 crore in FY25 to INR 73-74 crore in FY26 on lower interest income from QIP funds; management deferred the reconciliation offline, so a reversal is uncertain.

532163|2026-06.headline: Saregama Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27% YoY to Rs 263.6 crore and adjusted EBITDA 69% to Rs 112.4 crore; music vertical grew 39%.
532163|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 263.6 crore (+27% YoY), adjusted EBITDA Rs 112.4 crore (+69% YoY) and operational PBT Rs 70.5 crore (+38% YoY). The music vertical (licensing, artiste management, retail) delivered Rs 230.6 crore revenue (+39%), EBITDA Rs 139.8 crore (+36%) and net margin Rs 99.6 crore (+31%). Video revenue fell 52% to about Rs 17 crore as the company winds down its films business in favour of Bhansali Productions. Management reiterated 20-23% music growth and 60-65% music EBITDA margin guidance, and asked analysts to judge performance on a rolling 12-month basis.

Rs 40 crore per quarter run rate over last three quarters

segments.name: Live Events

segments.commentary: Reached breakeven in FY26 and is moving towards profitability in FY27; no revenue figure disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp QoQ jump in YouTube views and what is the outlook for brand tie-ups?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give specifics, attributing swings to album performance and asking for 12-month rolling review; brand selling is now a single joint team across the company.

qa_highlights.question: Why did music EBITDA margin fall about 1% YoY despite 40%+ revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to mix, as lower-margin Artiste Management grew faster; core licensing margins unchanged, with short-term pressure from rising content investment.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income decline sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash was diverted to Bhansali Productions investments, reducing other income.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the difference in content spend between the Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 cash flow statements (Rs 186 crore vs Rs 265 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Not answered on the call; management said it would take the query offline.

qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share the figure, citing competition sensitivity.

532163|2026-09.headline: Saregama Q2 FY27 revenue rose 37% YoY to INR3,143 million and adjusted EBITDA rose 39% to INR1,180 million.
532163|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of INR3,143 million (+37% YoY), adjusted EBITDA of INR1,180 million (+39%) and operational PBT of INR858 million (+43%). The music vertical (licensing, artist management, retail) grew 35% YoY to INR2,513 million, with EBITDA of INR1,540 million. Management repeatedly asked investors to judge performance on a rolling 12-month basis, citing a low base in H1 FY26. The video vertical revenue fell 16% to INR183 million as the film business is wound down in favour of Bhansali Productions.

532174|2026-03.headline: ICICI Bank Q4 FY26 PBT ex-treasury rose 10.1% YoY to ₹18,209 crore, with provisions falling to just ₹96 crore.
532174|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 profit before tax excluding treasury grew 10.1% YoY to ₹18,209 crore and profit after tax grew 8.5% to ₹13,702 crore, helped by provisions of only ₹96 crore versus ₹891 crore in Q3. Core operating profit grew only 5.1% YoY as operating expenses rose 12.0%, so the bottom line leaned on low credit costs and recoveries from written-off accounts. Loan growth accelerated to 15.8% YoY, led by rural (+25.6%), business banking (+24.4%) and mortgages (+13.2%), while deposits grew 11.4%. Management declined to guide on loan growth and said NIM should stay range-bound in FY27, while flagging West Asia conflict uncertainty without yet seeing portfolio stress.

Mortgage pickup attributed to better disbursements after benchmark stabilised, not lower prepayments.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 8.5% PAT growth came from low provisions versus core income?
qa_highlights.answer: Core operating profit grew 5.1% in Q4 and 7.7% in FY26; provisions fell about 89-90% YoY and PBT ex-treasury grew about 10%. Management said treasury was little changed.

qa_highlights.question: Will deposit rates rise, given recent falls?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rate direction depends on macro conditions and it is difficult to make a long-term call; the bank focuses on CASA and primary-banking relationships.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the mortgage pickup and does the deposit-loan gap persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Mortgage growth reflects benchmark stability and better disbursements. Average deposit growth (about 10.8%) is close to average loan growth, and LCR is about 125-126%, so deposits will not constrain loans.

qa_highlights.question: Was there any provision release or write-back this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower retail net additions, moderating unsecured slippages, and higher corporate recoveries including recoveries from written-off accounts drove the low provisions. Contingency and agri standard asset provisions were not used.

qa_highlights.question: Is the sub-50 bps credit cost sustainable into FY27, given the West Asia conflict?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is difficult to forecast given the lack of clarity, and it will focus on good-quality customers and monitor developments. It sees no cause for concern in retail, and business banking is being monitored.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the credit card business and its market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Card book fell 5.6% YoY; management attributed the decline to spends and revolver levels, exited riskier segments, and said profitability remains healthy. It gave no market share figure.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: supply shocks, energy prices, and corporate and MSME stress, with management saying it is too early to call and the Dubai and Bahrain presence being monitored.
Provisions at ₹96 crore are unlikely to be repeated; they were helped by one-off corporate recoveries from written-off accounts, so credit cost normalisation is a risk.
Core operating profit growth of 5.1% and opex growth of 12.0% show negative jaws in Q4; management wants opex growth below income growth.
Deposit repricing and NIM range-bound outlook as cost of deposits falls; government SA balances in low-teens share of SA balances.

532174|2026-06.headline: ICICI Bank Q1 FY27: PBT excluding treasury rose 20.9% YoY to ₹18,975 crore; NIM 4.36%, loans up 19.6% YoY.
532174|2026-06.overview: ICICI Bank posted strong Q1 FY27 profit growth, with PBT excluding treasury up 20.9% YoY to ₹18,975 crore and PAT up 15.9% to ₹14,805 crore. Net interest margin expanded to 4.36% from 4.32% in Q4, helped by about 8 bps from income tax refund interest; excluding that, NIM was 4.28%. Loan growth accelerated to 19.6% YoY, led by a sequential pickup in domestic corporate (up 6.9% QoQ) and business banking, while asset quality was stable with net NPA at 0.35%. Management guided NIM to be range-bound in FY27 but flagged possible dilution from the FCNR(B) mobilisation push, and gave no FCNR amounts raised so far.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 4.36% NIM sustainable and what levers exist, and what drove the slippage rise and West Asia stress?

qa_highlights.question: How much has been mobilised under FCNR(B), at what leverage, and will rates go above 6%?
qa_highlights.answer: No amount or leverage disclosed; management said rates will be calibrated, funding will come from partner banks, bond issuance and unleveraged inflows, and no need to raise rates above 6% currently. Details expected with Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is 20% loan growth sustainable and where is the corporate demand coming from?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth reflects system momentum from policy measures, that there are no segment targets, and that corporate demand reflects working capital needs and bond/equity market moderation. Average loan growth will be somewhat lower than the period-end rate.

qa_highlights.answer: One NCLT-driven recovery on an asset previously sold to NARCL came through this quarter. Reported credit cost 32 bps; normalised about 50 bps excluding chunky recoveries.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving fee income growth and card/personal loan trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Fee growth reflects broad business momentum plus a low base; sequential fee increase about ₹500 crore. Personal loans grew 12% YoY and 4% QoQ; cards growth is weak due to lower revolver rates.

qa_highlights.question: What is the LCR and NRI share of deposits, and surplus SLR?

Management said competitive intensity is unchanged, not materially higher QoQ.

Credit card decline is attributed to festive-season spend timing; management expects growth from Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 18 bp NIM decline and where does it stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the fall from 4.28% (ex-tax-refund) to 4.18% to FCNR(B) inflows, lower CASA ratio, higher overseas book share and retail term deposits. Full impact lands in Q3, with margins rising from Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the $18 billion FCNR(B) was deployed and where?

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the proposed IRDAI insurance distribution guidelines on fee income?

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Q2 treasury turn into a loss?

qa_highlights.question: What were the Q2 slippages and write-offs?

qa_highlights.question: Is corporate loan growth sustainable, and is it temporary FCNR parking?

532175|2026-03.headline: Cyient DET Q4 FY26 revenue $163.5M, down 2.4% QoQ in constant currency; INR720 crore buyback at INR1,125/share announced.

Normalized DET EBIT margin held at 12.4% and gross margin rose 114 bps QoQ to 38.9%. Management announced a buyback of up to 6.4M shares (5.76%) at INR1,125 per share for up to INR720 crore, and a planned fundraise at Cyient Semiconductor. The company also paused Project Astro, an acquisition, and took a INR71 crore exceptional diligence charge.

532175|2026-06.headline: Cyient Q1 FY27: DET revenue $162.5M, down 0.5% QoQ in constant currency, while DET EBIT margin rose to 13.2% and the 15% target slipped to H1 FY28.

Normalized DET EBIT margin expanded to 13.2% (+79 bps QoQ, +114 bps YoY) on cost optimisation and a stronger USD. Management pushed out its 15% EBIT target from Q4 FY27 to around H1 FY28 because revenue ramp-up is lagging, and it said mid-single-digit FY27 growth is now hard to achieve. Group revenue was $219M (+4.5% QoQ, +9.1% YoY in constant currency), with Kinetic Technologies consolidated for the first time.

segments.commentary: Management said the quarter closed with its highest-ever order book and book-to-bill above 1.5, with double-digit EBITDA margins for four consecutive quarters. No DLM financial figures were given on the call.

532178|2026-03.headline: Engineers India FY26 standalone turnover rose 27% to Rs.3,849 crore and PAT 37% to Rs.638 crore; order book hit a record Rs.15,109 crore.
532178|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a record year: standalone turnover Rs.3,849 crore (+27% YoY), PAT Rs.638 crore (+37%), operating margin 16.22% (vs 14.76%), and EPS Rs.11.36 (vs Rs.8.28). Q4 turnover was Rs.899 crore with PBT Rs.195 crore and PAT Rs.152 crore. Order inflow was Rs.7,979 crore versus Rs.8,214 crore a year earlier, while the order book reached Rs.15,109 crore (Rs.11,717 crore a year earlier). Management flagged a slowdown in Middle East awards due to the regional conflict, while domestic and Africa activity was steady, and guided FY27 consultancy margins of 20-25% and LSTK margins of 5-7%.

segments.name: Consultancy & engineering
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover Rs.1,782 crore (vs Rs.1,678 crore); Q4 turnover Rs.489 crore with a reported Q4 margin near 29%, which management attributed to a Rs.221 crore change order, not a one-off write-back. Guided segment margin 20-25%.

segments.name: Turnkey (LSTK)
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover Rs.2,067 crore (vs Rs.1,349 crore); Q4 turnover Rs.410 crore. Guided segment margin 5-7%. Dangote refinery (USD 360 million) and fertilizer (USD 70 million, four lines) contracts are being executed, started around January 2026.

segments.name: Subsidiary CEIL
segments.commentary: Profit rose to Rs.24.71 crore in FY26 from Rs.20.62 crore. Associate (refinery-linked) profit was about Rs.40 crore in the latest quarter after a shutdown-affected earlier period; management expects 100% plant capacity this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 order inflow to stay around Rs.8,000 crore (consultancy plus LSTK), with an aim to exceed it; management said FY27 inflow is hard to predict beyond one or two quarters.
FY27 revenue growth guided at a minimum of 10-15%, based on two months of the year elapsed.
Consultancy segment margin to be sustained at 20-25%; LSTK segment margin at 5-7%.
Consultancy revenue growth seen conservatively at 15-20% a year over the next two to three years.
Middle East: management expects a delay of a couple of months in big-ticket awards; Africa and the new Saudi Aramco agreements (5+3 years) are the growth routes.
Final dividend of Rs.2.5 per share proposed; with the interim Rs.2.5, total FY26 dividend is Rs.5 per share (100% of face value Rs.5).
capex_capacity: Dangote refinery and fertilizer projects are about four years in duration; site activity expected to start around end-2026 or early 2027.
Andhra (BPCL) project: feasibility underway; licensor selection next, with project activities targeted in FY27.
IOCL Paradip phase-2 balance order (about Rs.8-10 billion) expected to be awarded by end of FY27, after the investment decision.
Panipat (P25) project is in advanced construction and expected to commission soon.
Company is setting up a CBG plant in Maharashtra on its own investment and is the OT consultant for an MRPL sustainable aviation fuel plant.
demand_pricing: Order book is at a record Rs.15,109 crore, but FY26 inflow was slightly lower than FY25 at Rs.7,979 crore.
Middle East is about 30% of overseas business secured, and roughly 10-15% of the current order book. Big-ticket Middle East awards are slower, with client decisions delayed by security concerns.
Africa is the main overseas focus after the Dangote awards; management sees investment shifting to Africa as an alternative hub.
Infrastructure is about 25% of FY26 order inflow (clients include ONGC, NTPC, Government of Rajasthan, IIMs/IITs and data centres).
Coal gasification: government raised viability gap funding; a consultancy opportunity of about Rs.300-400 crore was indicated. Project sizes of Rs.10,000-40,000 crore were cited.
Public-sector tenders are competitive or negotiated; hit rate on bids is about 20-25%. Nomination only for critical projects.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for FY27 consultancy inflow in domestic and international markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to sustain inflow at roughly the current level of about Rs.8,000 crore total; Middle East slowdown is the key risk, with domestic projects not being delayed or cancelled.

qa_highlights.question: Middle East share of the order book and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Middle East is about 30% of overseas business secured and 10-15% of the current order book; a Saudi Aramco long-term agreement (5+3 years) was signed, with an out-of-kingdom agreement pending.

qa_highlights.question: Was there any one-off or change order behind Q4 consultancy margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no write-offs; a Rs.221 crore change order was received in FY26 and the expenditure already incurred, and the Q4 margins are described as normalised.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue slippage Q4 vs Q3 and cost pressures?
qa_highlights.answer: No revenue slippage; the prior quarter included a change order over Rs.200 crore, which made it high-profit. Management did not report commodity cost impacts.

qa_highlights.question: Expected growth in FY27 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Minimum 10-15% growth expected in FY27 execution; FY27 and FY28 revenue guidance was deferred to next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Middle East and Africa opportunity size?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs.1,000-2,000 crore of projects is achievable over time, with an inflection expected around FY27-FY29.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict delaying big-ticket awards and revamp-led spending; monitor Saudi and out-of-kingdom agreement signing.
Consultancy order inflow, with FY26 slightly below FY25 and the Rs.8,000 crore FY27 target dependent on public-sector tenders.
Sustainability of 20%+ consultancy margins; Q4 margin benefited from a Rs.221 crore change order.
Dangote and IOCL Paradip conversion timing; large LSTK jobs carry 5-7% margins.

532178|2026-06.headline: Engineers India Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 55% to INR109 crores, while turnover fell 7% to INR801 crores on Turnkey decline.

Turnkey turnover fell to INR302 crores from INR449 crores as major projects tapered. Order book stood at INR14,424 crores at 30 June 2026, but Q1 order inflow was only INR514 crores. Management kept the INR8,000 crore FY27 order inflow target and the FY27 operating margin guidance of 16%, and said the Middle East new-mega-project pipeline has slowed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR8,000 crore order inflow target still achievable, and how much would be consultancy?

qa_highlights.question: Will there be write-backs or change orders this year, including HPCL Barmer?

qa_highlights.question: How will revenue be recognised on the Dangote Nigeria order?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is recognised on cost-progress basis, with turnover booked as cost progress is achieved over about 4 years.

Management expects H2 FY27 ROA of about 1.40% or better, driven by recoveries from written-off accounts, a special OTS scheme, treasury, fee income and non-fund-based business.
NIM expected to improve substantially from Q3 as the 25 bps repo cut passes through, high-cost deposits are shed, and the repo rate may rise further. No numerical NIM guidance given.
Employee cost expected flat to slightly lower over the next two quarters, returning to current levels in FY28 after hiring.
Credit cost expected to stay around INR70-85 crore per quarter; ECL transition impact to be quantified by December board/next quarter. Management says the ECL hit will be below the industry average.
Capital raise planned: INR1,000 crore equity (timing dependent on market conditions) and INR500 crore debt (expected this quarter).
About 65% of loans are repo-linked and 31% MCLR-linked; repo changes passed through the same day.
capex_capacity: Capital raise planned: INR1,000 crore equity (timing dependent on market conditions; approval already in place, team says it is ready) and INR500 crore debt (expected this quarter).
Capital position at 30 Sep 2026: CRAR 16.57%, CET1 13.88%; RoA 1.07% and RoE 13.68% for Q2.
Employee cost expected flat to slightly lower over the next two quarters due to retirements; new hiring to be completed by end of Q3 or early Q4 FY27, taking cost back to current levels in FY28.
Two life insurance partners added (SBI Life, HDFC Life) to expand third-party product sales; management expects volume growth to offset IRDAI commission reductions.
Retail is the growth focus; management targets 60% of FY27 credit growth from retail and 40% from corporate, with about 18% credit growth aimed for if retail momentum continues.
demand_pricing: Retail and RAM led growth; management says retail is preferred for its higher yield.

Term deposit growth continues to outpace CASA, in line with industry trend. Deposit growth YTD about 7% against 10% guidance (now 12%+ for year). CASA inflows turned positive in Q2 after a sharp Q1 outflow.
Q1 CASA outflows were largely converted to term deposits within the bank, according to management; average and period-end balances are now close.
High-cost CDs of about 8% were taken in Q1 to fund loan commitments; most has been repaid. Remaining high-cost bulk deposits are under INR3,000 crore.
Non-fund-based business up about 30-40% QoQ. Two more life insurers added (SBI Life, HDFC Life); management expects volume growth to offset IRDAI commission cuts.
Government and salary-account MoUs: more than 20 organisations signed in the last quarter; a new 5-year Government of J&K salary MoU is expected to be signed the day after the call.

qa_highlights.question: What steps are being taken to improve the CASA mix, which lags term deposit growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited salary-account MoUs with 20+ organisations, tighter monitoring of UPI POS and QR merchant routing, and a new 5-year Government of J&K salary MoU. It says CASA is at least held at around 42%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the credit cost outlook, and what is the ongoing cost after ECL?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify the ECL impact until the end of next quarter, with the model going to the December board. It sees no reason for credit cost to rise; current provisions are ageing-based and H1 slippages were INR234 crore versus INR550 crore a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Why was ROA guidance lowered to about 1.2%, and is H2 ROA of 1.4% achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is conservative and the guidance is '1.20 plus', not a downgrade. It expects H2 ROA of about 1.40%, and possibly better, supported by written-off account recoveries and an OTS scheme.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 credit growth of 14% realistic versus 24-25% currently?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 14% is a conservative floor ('14% plus'), with an aim of around 18%. It does not expect 25%, since Q3 and Q4 of last year were strong comparators.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NIM outlook and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no numerical NIM target but said it will rise substantially from Q3. Drivers are the 25 bps repo pass-through, the end of high-cost deposits, higher yields, and possible further rate hikes. About 65% of the book is repo-linked and 31% MCLR-linked.

qa_highlights.question: What was the one-off treasury gain, and how much was recovered from TWO accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: TWO recoveries were INR25 crore in the quarter. A post-quarter equity stake sale and revaluation gain of about INR100 crore is not in Q2. AFS reserve movement was negative INR62 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ECL transition hit quantified, and how prepared is the bank?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ECL hit will be below the industry average and the bank holds about INR300 crore of buffer. The model is nearly ready and will go to the board in December, when the transitional range will be given.

risks_watch: ECL transition impact is not yet quantified; the range is due in December and the model goes to the board then. Analysts flagged high SMA-0/1/2 (about 5% SMA-1+2).
FY28 ROA sustainability depends on recoveries from written-off accounts and the OTS scheme; management has not quantified these.
NIM improvement is not quantified; cost of deposits rose to 4.85% and yield on advances is flat at 8.55%.
Insurance commission will fall under new IRDAI rules; management expects volume growth to offset this.
Equity raise (INR1,000 crore) timing is open; debt raise (INR500 crore) is expected this quarter.
Q1 CASA outflow has not been fully reversed; CASA ratio is 41.97% against a 42%+ target.
532209|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and on the direction of NIM and other income, but guarded on numbers: no NIM figure and no ECL quantum. Management pushed back on the ROA-downgrade framing and called the 14% credit growth guide conservative.
key_quotes: I am 100% sure the NIM is going to go up. I'm not predicting a number, but it is going to go up substantially.
It is not a one-off factor. It is going to continue.
I will give that range in the month of December. I'll give you exact number.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Advances grew 23.7% YoY and deposits 16.3% YoY; FY27 guidance is credit growth 14%+ and deposit growth 12%+, with Q2 net incremental credit entirely from RAM.

532210|2026-03.headline: City Union Bank Q4 FY26: advances up 26% YoY to INR66,698 crore and PAT up 25% to INR360 crore, with gross NPA at 1.91%.
532210|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the bank's strongest quarter in recent years, with total business growing about 24% YoY and advances up 26% to INR66,698 crore. Asset quality kept improving: gross NPA fell to 1.91% from 3.09% a year earlier, and total SMA fell to 2.47% from 3.68% in Q3. Q4 PAT rose 25% to INR360 crore, the highest single quarter, and FY26 PAT rose 18% to INR1,326 crore with ROA at 1.56%. The call also marked the handover of MD and CEO from Dr. N. Kamakodi to R. Vijay Anandh effective 1 May 2026.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loans are about 30% of the book and growing faster than overall loans; management says the 30% level is near the upper limit, with 1-2% flexibility. Per-gram lending was capped around INR10,000-10,500 even at peak gold prices.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Core focus segment, with management citing rising capacity utilisation and CC limit usage as demand drivers. FY27 plan keeps MSME at 55-60% of the mix. Only 3-4% of MSME loans are under CGTMSE cover.

segments.name: Secured retail
segments.commentary: Housing and loans against property are growing and are an additional growth driver. FY27 plan uses secured retail to fill the remaining share of the mix after MSME and gold.

guidance_outlook: FY27 advances growth planned at 2-3% above industry credit growth, with MSME at 55-60%, gold loans and secured retail as additional enhancers.
FY27 NIM expected to stay in a narrow 5-10 bps band around the FY26 level of 3.74%.
FY27 operating expenses expected to rise 15-18% YoY, with about 75 branches to be opened in FY27 (about 50 in April, 25 by year-end).
ROA to exit FY27 at least 10 bps higher, at about 1.65-1.67%, supported by retail income and lower cost-to-income.
CD ratio to be kept at 85-87%. Third-party business to be 1-2% of the book. Fee income to be 55-60% of other income.

Credit cost expected to fall about 50% from the 15-year average of about 0.60% over the next 15 years; individual years may vary. Management said the ECL circular lets banks adjust the opening balance, so the ECL impact on P&L is expected to be limited.
capex_capacity: Branch network reached 1,000 with the opening of the 1,000th branch at Kumbakonam on 4 May 2026, up from about 950 at FY26 end.
About 75 branches to be opened in FY27, with about 50 in April 2026 (70 opened in the first month per the CEO-designate); branches typically reach breakeven in year one.
Distribution capacity was lifted by the Newgen LOS and digital process set, which the management credits for secured MSME and retail growth.
demand_pricing: Advances grew by over INR5,800 crore in Q1 FY26 and INR13,600 crore for the full year; double-digit growth has run for eight consecutive quarters.
Deposit growth was matched to credit growth, with CASA at 28% of deposits and the average CD ratio at 85% for FY26. Some CDs were replaced by retail term deposits.
Yield on advances was 9.80% in Q4 (9.73% in Q3) and 9.75% for FY26 (9.79% in FY25). The cost of deposits was 5.60% in Q4 (5.57% in Q3).
Management said rate passthrough was completed around December 2025, and incremental yields are holding up, with non-agri gold loans at double-digit yields.
Management is watching the US-Iran conflict and oil prices; no visible impact on asset quality so far. Management expects a 1-2% extra slippage rate in a downturn, mainly on new business.

qa_highlights.question: How does the bank manage risk on gold loans given a 10-15% gold price fall from the peak?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said per-gram lending was capped at about INR10,000-10,500 even when gold peaked at INR15,000-16,000, so there is a cushion. It cited a loss of about INR5 crore in the 2014 gold price crash.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cost of deposits rise 3 bps QoQ, and where will it go?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some deposit rates were fine-tuned by 10-25 bps to support fast credit growth. It said the 3-5 bps movement is noise from CASA rate variation and it can add INR3,000 crore of advances without new deposits.

qa_highlights.question: Will yield on advances keep falling after the rate cuts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rate passthrough is complete, and roughly 30% of the book is fixed-rate gold. Incremental book of about INR5,000 crore booked in H2 was at higher yields, which held the margin.

qa_highlights.question: When does ROA move to 1.7-1.8%?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO-designate said FY27 exit ROA should be 1.65-1.67%, at least 10 bps above the FY26 level, based on retail income and lower cost-to-income.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for steady-state credit costs after the ECL norms?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said the 15-year average credit cost is about 0.60%, and FY25 and FY26 were 0.09% and 0.04%. He expects at least a 50% reduction over the long run, with AI-based underwriting cited as the reason.

qa_highlights.question: Will underwriting filters tighten given fuel prices and demand risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it watches SMA trends and branch and customer feedback. It would add some caution to filters but has no plan to change them now, as underwriting is set for multiple business cycles.

risks_watch: Gold price correction on the INR30%+ gold book and whether LTV cushions hold.
Impact of the US-Iran conflict and oil prices on MSME demand and slippages; management expects an extra 1-2% slippage in a downturn.
Rising deposit costs as the bank fine-tunes rates to fund faster credit growth; the CD ratio is at 85% and CASA at 28%.
Opex growth of 15-18% in FY27 from branch expansion, against the ROA target of 1.65-1.67%.
Leadership transition: MD and CEO handover on 1 May 2026, plus the retirement of two independent directors in February 2026. The retiring MD's future non-executive board role depends on RBI approval.
532210|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY26 delivery and asset quality, with management saying it met all earlier guidance. More cautious on macro risks, particularly the US-Iran conflict and fuel prices. Evasive on the ECL steady-state credit cost, deferring that question to the CEO-designate.
key_quotes: By and large, almost all the expectations whatever we shared with you in the earlier con-calls for the financial year 2026 were met in the same spirit whatever we had shared with you.
The gross NPA has come below 2 % mark after 11 years.
I think we should exit this year with at least 10 bps more in ROA, so we should be there between 1.65% to 1.67%.

rows.why: Leadership changed on 1 May 2026, and the retiring MD's future non-executive board role depends on RBI approval.

532210|2026-06.headline: City Union Bank Q1 FY27 PAT rose 25% YoY to Rs 383 crore, a record, with GNPA down to 1.73% and NIM guided to 3.65-3.70%.
532210|2026-06.overview: Advances grew 25% YoY to Rs 67,645 crore and deposits 21% to Rs 79,342 crore, with CD ratio at 85%. Operating profit rose 29% to Rs 581 crore and PAT 25% to Rs 383 crore, both stated as record highs. Asset quality improved further: GNPA 1.73% (from 2.99% a year ago), Net NPA 0.61%, and recoveries exceeded slippages. Management guided to a moderate NIM dip from higher cost of funds, cost-to-income of 47-48% for FY27, and an exit ROA of 1.60-1.65%.

financial_highlights.change: up 25% QoQ as stated; vs Rs 54,020 crore in 1QFY26

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME average disbursement about Rs 3,500 crore per quarter; management targets MSME at 55-60% of book and growth 2-3% above system. Average utilisation fell from 73% to 70%; repayments about Rs 900 crore per month.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Share of book at 30-31%, guided to stay 31-32%. Agri gold yield about 10-10.5% and non-agri 11-11.5%; agri priced 100 bps lower. Average LTV 62.07%. Branches rose from 700 to 1,000.

segments.name: Retail secured (LAP)
segments.commentary: LAP yield about 9.60-9.70%. Management expects retail secured at about 10% of book.

segments.name: Investments
segments.commentary: Yield on investments fell to 6.42% from 6.61% in 4QFY26 because Rs 12 crore of mutual fund income (on about Rs 700 crore invested) was classified under other income; 6.67% on an interest-income basis.

guidance_outlook: Advances growth guided at 2-3% above industry credit growth for FY27; DSA business about 1-2% of book.
NIM expected at 3.65-3.70% over the next few quarters as cost of deposits rises about 5 bps; long-term view 3.70-3.75%.
Cost of deposits guided at 5.60-5.70%; borrowing cost of about Rs 94 crore per quarter for the next two quarters.
Cost-to-income guided at 47-48% for FY27 (currently 45%) because staff hikes start from July; long-term aspiration below 45% in about three years.
Exit ROA guided at 1.60-1.65%; full-year ROA 1.55-1.65%. Steady-state credit cost about 0.40%; FY27 slippages Rs 700-750 crore; slippage ratio 1.20-1.30%.
ECLGS participation: Rs 800 crore disbursed to date; total expected Rs 2,000-2,500 crore. ECL provisioning about 0.45% of loan book, CAR consumption capped at 0.65%.
capex_capacity: Branch rollout front-loaded this year; branch count rose from 700 to 1,000 in the gold-loan context.
AI-led automation invested in operations; management expects it to lower cost further.
Liquidity: average LCR at 150%.

Business enterprise (non-MSME, no Udyam registration) loans at Rs 18,827 million; large-industry book fell from Rs 22,500 million (Dec-25) to about Rs 15,000 million then rose to Rs 19,000 million on exits and yield pressure.
demand_pricing: Gold loan rates unchanged; management ruled out raising rates to slow growth, citing agri customer needs and competitiveness in non-agri gold; rates up 20-25 bps over last year.
MSME utilisation fell to 70% from 73-74% norm; management attributes it to cautious borrowers and sees it recovering with textile demand after the European trade agreement.
Term deposit rates expected to rise on high demand; FCNR window brought in fresh deposits of Rs 150 crore.
SMA-0/1/2 at 1.20%/0.70%/0.90% (total 2.85%), down from 7.12% in June 2025 and 10.78% in September 2024. Domestic consumption said to be insulated from West Asia stress.
Fee income fell about 15% YoY and 19% in one comparison per analyst question; management expects catch-up in Q2-Q4 from processing fees, suit recoveries and insurance.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins move beyond the near-term cost-of-funds increase (FY27-FY28 levers), given stagnant lending yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to MSME, gold and retail secured yields (agri gold ~10-10.5%, non-agri 11-11.5%, LAP 9.60-9.70%, MSME 9.30-9.40%) and a low-cost deposit franchise; long-term NIM view 3.70-3.75%. The Q1 cost-of-funds decline was attributed to better repricing and lower borrowing cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why is MSME growing about 15% when system MSME growth is above 20%? Is utilisation falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Rs 900 crore monthly repayments, MSME utilisation down to 70% from a 73-74% norm, and slightly more cautious pricing. Guidance is MSME growth 2-3% above system, with MSME at 55-60% of book.

qa_highlights.question: What slippage and credit cost levels are sustainable over one to two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Steady-state credit cost about 0.40%; FY27 slippages Rs 700-750 crore; slippage ratio 1.20-1.30%. Recoveries have exceeded slippages for about 10 quarters and are expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: How will the bank reach 25-30% higher growth with the mix intact (gold 31-32%, MSME 55-60%, retail 10%), and what is the MSME outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the mix targets and said lower utilisation cost about 3-4% of MSME growth. It expects MSME growth 2-3% above system, with the European trade agreement seen supporting textile utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in cost of funds despite lower deposit costs, and what is the treasury and borrowing cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowing cost rose to Rs 94 crore from Rs 72.5 crore in 4QFY26; treasury gains were Rs 52.54 crore vs Rs 29 crore in 4QFY26. Borrowing cost is guided at about Rs 94 crore per quarter for the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How is the bank participating in ECLGS, and how is the ECL provisioning assessed?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 800 crore disbursed to date (Rs 200 crore last quarter); total expected Rs 2,000-2,500 crore. ECL provision about 0.45% of loan book, with CAR consumption capped at 0.65%; flow impact described as negligible given the secured book.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fee income decline and how will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Fee income was down about 15% YoY (analyst cited 19% in one comparison). Management expects catch-up in Q2-Q4 from processing fees, suit recoveries and insurance income; non-treasury other income was Rs 243 crore in Q1 vs roughly Rs 300 crore in Q4 last year.

risks_watch: Utilisation trend in MSME (70% in Q1 vs 73-74% norm) and whether the European trade-agreement recovery in textiles materialises.
Cost of deposits moving to 5.60-5.70% and the ~5 bps NIM hit; NIM guided 3.65-3.70%, below the 3.78% reported in Q1.
Cost-to-income rising to 47-48% for FY27 from 45.42% as staff hikes start from July; exit ROA 1.60-1.65% depends on fee income recovery.
Gold loan pricing: management ruled out rate hikes, so growth is supported only by volume; agri gold LTV around 62% with sensitivity to gold price drops.
West Asia stress and SMA trends (SMA-0/1/2 total 2.85%) and ECLGS-linked disbursements that may affect future asset quality.
Large-industry book volatility (Rs 22,500 million in Dec-25, down to ~Rs 15,000 million, then ~Rs 19,000 million) and the non-MSME business enterprise book of Rs 18,827 million.
key_quotes: For 1QFY27 as well, we have achieved 25% credit growth quarter-on-quarter, the highest growth rate in June-to-June and our advances had increased to Rs. 67,645 crores from Rs. 54,020 crores in 1QFY26.
So, the trend of recovery more than slippages continues, and we are confident of maintaining recovery more than slippages for the next quarter as well, which is the current quarter.
So, we are quite confident of maintaining the cost-to-income at 47%. We are currently at 45 as we speak.
We haven't changed any rate of interest for gold loans. We are at the same rate, and we continue to do the same.
532210|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident and specific on asset quality, recoveries and growth targets, repeating FY27 guidance from the Q4 call. It was cautious on margins, cost-to-income and fee income, and deflected on the MSME utilisation decline and gold pricing rather than offering new numbers.

rows.why: NIM guided to 3.65-3.70% over the next few quarters from 3.78% in Q1, as cost of deposits rises about 5 bps to 5.60-5.70%; cost-to-income rising to 47-48% for FY27 from 45.42%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Gold-loan branches rose from 700 to 1,000 and the branch rollout is front-loaded this year, though no new plant or capex quantum was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Advances guided at 2-3% above industry credit growth for FY27; advances up 25% YoY to Rs 67,645 crore and deposits up 21% to Rs 79,342 crore, but MSME utilisation fell to 70% from 73-74%.

rows.why: Management held FY27 guidance (ROA 1.55-1.65%, cost-to-income 47-48%, slippages Rs 700-750 crore) and guided NIM lower, so no upgrade signalled.

rows.label: Term deposit rate increases on high demand
rows.why: Management expects term deposit rates to rise; cost of deposits guided to 5.60-5.70% from 5.56% in Q1, a ~5 bps hit to NIM.

rows.label: MSME utilisation recovery with textile demand
rows.why: MSME utilisation fell to 70% from 73-74% norm; management expects recovery after the European trade agreement, but this is conditional and not quantified.

rows.label: Fee income catch-up
rows.why: Fee income fell about 15% YoY; non-treasury other income was Rs 243 crore in Q1 vs roughly Rs 300 crore a year ago, and management expects catch-up from processing fees, suit recoveries and insurance.

tone.note: Management was confident on asset quality (GNPA 1.73%, recoveries above slippages for about 10 quarters) and held FY27 guidance, but cautious on NIM, cost-to-income and fee income; analysts pressed on MSME growth lagging the system (about 15% vs above 20%) and utilisation falling to 70%.

532210|2026-09.headline: City Union Bank Q2 FY27 PAT rose 27% YoY to INR 416 crores, with advances up 26% to INR 72,442 crores and Gross NPA down to 1.44%.
532210|2026-09.overview: Management reported a strong Q2 FY27: advances grew over INR 4,800 crores QoQ (over 7%) to INR 72,442 crores, deposits rose 21% YoY to INR 83,893 crores, and NIM expanded 9 bps QoQ to 3.87%. Asset quality improved sharply, helped by sale of INR 803 crores of technically written-off and live accounts to an ARC, with Gross NPA falling to 1.44% from 1.73%. Management guided NIM to 3.85-3.95% for Q3 and Q4, and addressed scrutiny on gold loan practices, LTV norms and ECL transition impact (about INR 300 crores, of which about INR 30 crores already provided).

financial_highlights.change: Up from 3.78% in Q1 FY27; H1 FY26 was 3.59%
Down from 1.73% in Q1 FY27 (29 bps); Net NPA 0.48% vs 0.9% a year ago
+35% YoY from INR 259 crores; includes ARC-related income
Created as buffer for economic uncertainty

segments.name: MSME

532218|2026-06.headline: South Indian Bank Q1 FY27 net profit rose 17% YoY to INR378 crore, with record NII of INR1,025 crore and NIM of 3.23%.
532218|2026-06.overview: Net profit grew 17% YoY to INR378 crore, and net interest income hit a record INR1,025 crore, up 23% YoY and INR110 crore QoQ. NIM recovered to 3.23%, up 28 bps QoQ and 20 bps YoY, helped by repricing of high-cost deposits, CASA growth and a 50% cut in bulk deposits. Gross advances grew 17% YoY and gross NPA fell to 1.38%. Non-interest income was soft: core fees fell to INR179 crore from INR191 crore in Q4, and management called this a one-off. Management said the call was the last for MD and CEO P.R. Seshadri, who is leaving.

segments.name: Business loans (MSME)
segments.commentary: Business loans rose to INR14,391 crore from INR12,660 crore; growth was 18% excluding a INR554 crore charge-off. Management said MSME growth was muted versus expectations this quarter.

segments.name: Mortgages, home and auto loans
segments.commentary: Mortgage loans grew 34% YoY, home loans 19% and auto loans 34%, excluding IBPC/DA impact.

segments.name: Corporate book

532221|2026-03.headline: Sonata Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue fell 17.7% QoQ to Rs 2,536.2 Cr, while PAT rose 25% QoQ to Rs 130.5 Cr on International margin gains.

532221|2026-06.headline: Sonata Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 10.6% YoY to Rs 3,279.1 Cr, but PAT fell 17.1% QoQ to Rs 108.6 Cr on Rs 35.4 Cr forex hit.
532221|2026-06.overview: International services revenue was flat QoQ in constant currency (+0.1%) at $82 million, while EBITDA margin fell to 15.4% from 20.2% as utilisation dropped to 88.5% on a delayed large-deal ramp-up, a one-time compensation benefit reversed, and AI talent investments rose. Domestic revenue was Rs 2,505.6 Cr with gross contribution up 4.2% QoQ and 14.5% YoY, and management said an OEM direct-billing risk has been partly reversed through contract renewals. Management reiterated an AI-native, engineering-led strategy and an AI order book of $21.4 million, but declined to give a steady-state EBITDA margin or formal guidance.

qa_highlights.answer: Management (Jagannathan) said it is confident domestic growth momentum will continue as past issues are behind it. Rajsekhar said the six value pools are customer engagement and ops transformation, agentic AI, legacy modernisation, AI-ready data, resilient AI backbone and AI-native service delivery; micro-verticals include payments, mortgage and lending, healthcare, clinical ops, logistics and retail manufacturing, and are sharpened existing areas rather than new ones.

qa_highlights.answer: Jagannathan attributed the lower top-10 share (51%) to growth in the 11-20 client bucket and new wins, with no discounts or productivity pass-through and no major top-10 account declining. qa_highlights.answer: Jagannathan said the BFSI share grew beyond expectations, so R&D as a percentage of revenue fell; this is not a standalone R&D issue. Rajsekhar said TMT growth will come from hyperscalers and enterprise product and packaged software organisations, with early pipeline signs from new leadership.

qa_highlights.answer: Jagannathan said the normalised ETR is about 25%; Q1 benefited from a one-time US state R&D tax credit that reduces the cash tax liability.

532234|2026-03.headline: NALCO FY26 revenue rose 6.28% to Rs.17,843 crore and PAT 9.22% to Rs.5,816 crore, with FY27 alumina guidance of about 25 lakh tons.
532234|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as the best ever year on physical output, sales and financials, with revenue from operations up 6.28% to Rs.17,843 crore, EBITDA up 8.72% to Rs.8,613 crore and PAT up 9.22% to Rs.5,816 crore. Alumina realisation fell from about $580/t (FY25) to about $370/t (FY26), offset by higher volumes and a metal realisation rise to about $2,700/t. Management guided to lower alumina prices of $300-310/t for FY27 and LME averaging around $3,000-3,100/t as Middle East smelter curtailments unwind. The 5th stream refinery (2 lakh t) is scheduled for commissioning from June 2026, with the smelter and captive power plant project (0.5 mtpa) planned for ordering in FY27.

Domestic sales rose to about 1.37-1.4 lakh t from 40,000 t, exports about 13.09 lakh t.

segments.commentary: FY26 cast metal production about 4.71 lakh t (+2.61%), capacity 4.6 lakh t; FY27 plan 4.73 lakh t. Pricing is linked to LME with export premium fixed via six-monthly export tenders; no hedging. Q1 FY27 realisation guided at about $3,500-3,600/t for the quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 alumina production and sales planned at about 25 lakh t, around 2 lakh t above FY26; management said 2 lakh t is the minimum and could reach 3-3.5 lakh t depending on commissioning.
FY27 alumina realisation expected at $300-310/t average, with spot at $310-320/t; management cited surplus from Indonesian refineries and Middle East smelter curtailments.
FY27 LME average expected around $3,000-3,100/t once the Middle East supply disruption normalises; spot LME was about $3,550-3,600/t in April 2026.
Management expects FY27 PBT to stay above about Rs.2,000 crore per quarter run-rate if volumes hold and cost does not rise; alumina price decline seen as offset by metal prices.
Employee cost guided lower in FY27 as about 250 superannuations are offset by recruitment; pay revision impact of 10-15% expected from January 2027 (FY28 onwards).

Capex: about Rs.2,000 crore in FY26-27, Rs.4,000-5,000 crore in FY27-28, peaking at Rs.8,000-10,000 crore in FY28-30 for the 0.5 mtpa smelter (about Rs.17,000-18,000 crore) and power plant (about Rs.12,000 crore, to be shared 50:50 with NLC JV).
capex_capacity: 5th stream alumina refinery (2 lakh t): commissioning to start June 2026, taking 3-4 months to reach 50-60% of rated capacity; about one to two months delay possible. Capital work in progress about Rs.6,300 crore, of which about Rs.5,500 crore relates to the 5th stream and is expected to be capitalised in FY27.

Proposed 0.5 mtpa aluminium smelter with 270 MW captive power plant: DPR and technology licensor under way; board approval targeted around Aug-Sep 2026; tendering 6-7 months; groundwork from around April-May 2027; completion targeted December 2030 to early 2031.
Power plant to be a 50:50 JV with Neyveli Lignite Corporation (MoU signed, advanced negotiations), with NLC's Talcher coal mine nearby for coal security.
Additional wire rod mill of about 60,000 t (roughly two years) and MI annealing furnace to lift rolled products from about 2,000 t/month to 2,500 t/month.
Utkarsh JV with Mishra Dhatu Nigam discontinued; the Board cited negative IRR on a Rs.4,500-5,000 crore capex plan.
Captive coal target 4.8 mt in FY27; EC clearance for the enhanced coal output expected in about three to four months.
demand_pricing: Middle East smelter curtailments (Qatalum, EGA, Dubal and one other, cut around 50%) reduced alumina demand; Middle East used to take about 40-50% of alumina exports.
Spot alumina tenders recently at $310-336/t; company is relying only on spot tenders with no long-term contracts at present. Recent long-term contract priced at 11-11.5% of LME versus 15-17% earlier.
Japan and Asian premiums rose sharply; NALCO's export premium is fixed for six months via tenders, with the next export tender expected within a month or two.
Domestic alumina sales target of 2.5-3 lakh t in FY27 (about 1.4 lakh t in FY26).

Aluminium cost of production about Rs.155,000-160,000/t (FY26 average about Rs.156,000/t); alumina cost about Rs.20,000-22,000/t.

qa_highlights.answer: FY26 exports about 13.09 lakh t and domestic about 1.37 lakh t. Middle East historically took 40-50% of exports, now sharply reduced; no volume impact yet per management.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the employee cost and other expenses jump in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said employee cost fell 18% to 15% YoY, with about 351 retirements and 358 inductions in FY26 saving about Rs.65 crore. Other expenses included about Rs.40 crore red mud pond provision and Rs.54 crore additional fly ash transport provision, which are non-cash.

qa_highlights.question: What are alumina and aluminium price expectations for FY27 and what is the margin effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Alumina $300-310/t average; LME about Rs.3,000-3,100/t on average. Management said the metal price gain (about $400/t vs FY26 at $3,000-3,100) would offset alumina decline; metal is about 73% of revenue vs 27% alumina.

qa_highlights.question: What is the coal mix and cost per tonne?
qa_highlights.answer: Total requirement 7.2 mt; captive 4.8 mt target FY27 (4.0 mt FY26); balance mainly FSA linkage from Coal India, with e-auction only 10-15%. Captive about Rs.1,500/t, linkage about Rs.1,800/t, e-auction about Rs.2,100/t.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the wage revision?
qa_highlights.answer: Pay revision from January 2027 expected to raise employee cost 10-15% (possibly 12-13%) in FY28; FY27 impact estimated around Rs.100 crore additional, per management. Per-tonne cost expected to fall with volume growth.

Input cost inflation in Q1 FY27: HFO up to about Rs.70,000/t from Rs.46,000, CP coke and CT pitch up to about Rs.57,000/t, caustic soda rising to about Rs.45,000/t; management said cost of production would rise but stay within Rs.160,000/t.

So, both areas in alumina and metal, we have looked for the growth.

Power: 1,080 MW JV with NLC (50:50), total cost about INR 12,000 crore, NALCO share about INR 6,000 crore with equity about INR 3,500 crore total and bank debt guaranteed by NALCO. Coal is sourced from NLC mines in Talcher.
Captive coal expansion: 4.8 Mt, EC expected in 2-3 months. Pottangi bauxite mine MDO appointed, but production is held up by local resistance over an 8 km access road.
Panchpatmali bauxite reserve about 110 Mt plus new mines of about 100-120 Mt, giving a 15-20 year balance life at about 8 Mtpa.
demand_pricing: Alumina spot prices rose on Rusal and Chinese refinery red-mud curtailments and higher New Guinea bauxite costs. About 60-70% of alumina goes to the Middle East.
Alumina realisation is now about 10-11% of LME, down from 14-15%. Management sees 11-12% as the long-run level.
Domestic aluminium premium rose to about $110/t from about $60/t, attributed to Middle East war supply disruption. Management expects it to hold or fall as the war eases.
Input costs: caustic soda about INR 45,000/t in Q1 rising to about INR 49,000/t in Q2, CP coke INR 66,000-70,000/t (vs INR 44,000 last year), HFO INR 75,000/t (vs INR 46,000 last year).
Industry metal deficit of about 0.88 Mt is cited, with LME forecast at $3,000-3,200/t for the rest of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the 5th Stream refinery commissioning delayed by about 6 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Mechanical completion slipped by 2-3 months. Over 50 packages are in progress and mechanical completion is targeted for September-end, followed by water runs and then production. Output of about 2 lakh tonnes of alumina is still targeted in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall, and will it stay low through FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Average CTC fell from about INR 36 lakh to INR 33 lakh due to superannuation of high-paid staff and entry-level hiring. Last year's provisions for leave and gratuity and lower PRP accruals also contributed, and the trend should continue for the next three quarters. Q4 will rise because of the pay revision.

qa_highlights.question: Will raw material cost inflation erode margins as aluminium prices soften?
qa_highlights.answer: Metal cost rose about INR 15,000-16,000/t from raw materials. Management said higher alumina prices (about $370/t against a $320 expectation) should offset this, and Q2 metal cost is guided at INR 1,70,000-1,72,000/t.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any LME-linked alumina term contract for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: The term contracts earlier this year priced at about 10% of LME and were cancelled. Management will only tender when it gets better percentages, around 12-14% of LME.

qa_highlights.question: Coal stocks and monsoon risk for the refineries?
qa_highlights.answer: Captive coal covers about 60-70% of smelter power needs at Angul. Refinery coal stock is only 2-3 days against a 10-15 day norm because of rake priority to power plants. Management expects improvement after summer.

qa_highlights.question: How will the smelter and power capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Total capex to FY31 is about INR 24,000 crore, with the JV's 30:70 debt-equity split. NALCO's cash reserves of about INR 10,500 crore and internal accruals of about INR 3,500 crore a year are expected to fund the smelter without new borrowing.

Refinery coal stock at 2-3 days against a 10-15 day norm during monsoon, dependent on rake allocation.
Pottangi mine start-up depends on the 8 km access road amid local resistance. Target is October 2026.
