532234|2026-09.headline: NALCO posted record H1 FY27 results: revenue INR11,143 crore, EBITDA INR5,539 crore, PAT INR3,837 crore (H1 PAT up 54% YoY).
532234|2026-09.overview: Management described H1 FY27 as the best half-yearly performance since inception on revenue, EBITDA, PBT and PAT, with Q2 net profit of INR1,835 crore up 28% YoY. Input costs rose sharply in H1 (caustic soda, CP coke, fuel oil/LDO), with power and fuel up about INR317 crore YoY, mainly from fuel oil use during coal shortages and rain-related moisture issues. Management expects H2 input costs to hold near H1 levels, with techno-economic gains and a 5th Stream refinery start targeted around end-December or early January. Alumina spot realisation is improving, with H2 average realisation guided at about INR35,000/t versus INR33,200/t in H1, while Middle East shipping disruption has cut export dispatches.

qa_highlights.question: Status of 5th Stream refinery, Pottangi mines and Utkal coal expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Refinery packages largely complete with integrated trials and production start targeted late December or early January; Pottangi mining delayed by tree felling and local resistance, expected to resolve in 2-3 months; Utkal FY27 target 4.8 Mt pending environmental clearance.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 margins hold at Q2 levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed stable margins for H2 citing refinery start (about INR150 crore PBT benefit), techno-economic gains (at least INR100 crore) and absence of the one-off royalty impact (about INR300-350 crore total uplift expected in H2).

qa_highlights.question: Why did power and fuel costs rise in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Rail rake diversion to integrated power plants cut coal supply, leaving coal stock at 1-2 days versus 15-day norm; moisture forced heavy fuel oil use (INR256 crore) and purchased power rose INR73 crore after captive power plant breakdowns.

qa_highlights.question: How much will input costs inflate in H2 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 costs expected at H1 levels or lower; input price inflation about 2-4% per year and employee cost impact from the pay revision from FY28; management expects margins to be maintained over the next 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for alumina prices and Middle East and Indonesian supply?
qa_highlights.answer: Expected spot prices around $370-380/t, not above about $350-400; excess supply of about 1.6 Mt in the market and new Indonesian and Vedanta capacity add pressure, partly offset by smelter restarts in the Middle East.

qa_highlights.question: Coal sourcing and FSA exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: FSA for about 6 Mt covers smelter needs; e-auction coal fell to 1.96 lakh t in H1 FY27 from 5.16 lakh t in FY26, with linkage coal and Utkal coal replacing it.

532259|2026-03.headline: APAR Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 26.7% YoY to INR6,603 crores; PAT of INR254 crores was INR285 crores before INR31 crores of one-offs.
532259|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR6,603 crores, with domestic sales up 33.6% and exports up 13.3% YoY. Reported PAT of INR254 crores (3.8% margin) included about INR31 crores of one-offs (gratuity/leave encashment, ECB mark-to-market, and a legal provision); management says the operating PAT was about INR285 crores, up around 14%. FY26 revenue was INR22,902 crores (+23.3%), EBITDA INR2,067 crores (9% margin) and PAT INR977 crores (4.3% margin). Management flagged a near-term slowdown from the Middle East war, metal and freight cost spikes, polymer shortages and project deferrals, while reiterating medium-term growth and raising FY27 capex to about INR1,500 crores.

FY26 revenue INR5,373 crores (+6%), EBITDA INR5,943/KL vs INR6,145/KL. Domestic transformer oil +12.2% for FY26.

segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR1,903 crores (+35% YoY); EBITDA INR202 crores at 10.6% margin (+34.5%). FY26 revenue INR6,220 crores (+25.8%), EBITDA INR633 crores at 10.2% margin; cables overtook oil as the second-largest segment. Order book about INR1,800 crores.

Middle East business expected to stay subdued until the war is resolved; Iraq conductor deliveries pushed out.

Section 232 duty is 25% on copper and aluminium cables and 50% on aluminium conductors, which management sees as giving landed-cost visibility.
Domestic HVDC transformer oil awards have just been made; conductor and oil supply for these projects is expected to come later, running through FY27-FY28.

Specialty polymer prices and availability were hit by the Middle East war, which limits near-term specialty cable order booking and will hurt volumes and margins.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the US data-centre opportunity, and how should FY27-28 US growth and the capex be read?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects strong US traction led by data centres, with RFQs rising and US demand for both cables and conductors growing; a larger US presence is expected in FY27. Management also said it is not seeing hyperscaler capacity blocking of the kind seen in fibre.

qa_highlights.question: How should FY27 conductor profitability be thought of?
qa_highlights.answer: Medium-to-long-term conductor EBITDA is guided at INR35,000-36,000/MT plus tailwinds; the company does not give next-year guidance and will update as visibility improves.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and the breakup of the INR1,500 crore FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is Conductor 90-95%, Cables 85-90%, Oil 65-70%. FY27 capex splits into about INR400 crores Conductor, INR200 crores Oil and INR850 crores Cables.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dependence on the Middle East for specialty oils, sourcing and sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Sourcing from Saudi Aramco's Yanbu refinery has continued without interruption. Shipments to Saudi Arabia and Kuwait stopped in March and April and resumed in May at higher freight; the Middle East business is expected to stay subdued until the war ends.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for premium conductor volumes and CTC exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Premium conductors were 45.8% of FY26 revenue and over 50% of the order book. CTC exports to Middle East manufacturers have started, with Europe and US approvals in progress.

qa_highlights.question: Will the capex raise cable volumes, and does domestic competition affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is fungible across specifications, and the capex is pulling forward spend toward the INR10,000 crore cable target. Management said new entrants may cost a few percentage points of EBITDA, but the market is growing.

532259|2026-06.headline: Apar Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 29.1% to INR6,591 crore and PAT rose 77.7% to INR467 crore, a record quarter.

PAT rose 77.7% to INR467 crore (7.1% margin), which management called the highest quarterly sales and profit in company history. Conductor volumes fell 6.7% as customers deferred manufacturing clearance on conventional conductors amid the aluminium price spike, while premium mix rose. Management declined to answer guidance, forecast or funding questions because of a pending shareholder approval for securities issuance.

532259|2026-09.headline: Apar Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 21.3% YoY to INR6,931 crore and EBITDA 57.8% to INR787 crore, with a record INR12,025 crore order book.

Conductor volumes fell 9.2% YoY on delayed TBCB clearances and metal-driven customer deferrals, while the oil division's margins were boosted by contract buying and volumes fell about 20%. Management expects Q3 and Q4 conductor volumes to beat H1 and the in-transit revenue to be recognised in Q3.

532281|2026-03.headline: HCLTech Q4 FY26 revenue fell 3.3% QoQ to $3,682M with FY27 guidance of 1%-4% cc growth, weighed by two US clients and a soft software quarter.
532281|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was $3,682M, down 3.3% QoQ but up 2.4% YoY in constant currency, with services flat QoQ and software down 28.1% QoQ on seasonality and delayed March deal decisions. Operating margin was 16.5% (17.7% ex-restructuring), and net income was $486M at 13.2% of revenue. Management cited cuts in discretionary telecom spend at two large US clients and two discontinued SAP programs, and guided FY27 revenue growth of 1%-4% cc with EBIT margin of 17.5%-18.5%, excluding two pending acquisitions. The company also extended its capital allocation policy for five years, committing to return at least 75% of net income.

532281|2026-06.headline: HCLTech Q1 FY27 revenue $3,650M, down 0.5% QoQ but up 2.6% YoY in constant currency; record Q1 net new TCV of $2.4B; FY27 guidance held at 1-4%.
532281|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was seasonally weak sequentially, with revenue down 0.5% QoQ and EBIT margin at 16.9% (up 39 bps QoQ, helped by lower restructuring). Services grew 3.5% YoY, with ITBS up 4.2% and ER&D up only 0.3% YoY after a 3.7% QoQ decline. Net new TCV of $2.4B was the highest ever Q1, excluding a mega deal signed in early July. Management kept FY27 organic guidance of 1-4% revenue and 17.5-18.5% margin, and announced entry into AI datacenters with an up to INR3,500 crore initial investment.

BFSI growth attributed to AI-native approach and wallet share gains with top financial services clients; Life Sciences and Healthcare declined on lapse of medical device regulatory work and US healthcare stress.

qa_highlights.question: What limits raising guidance given record Q1 bookings and the early-July mega deal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the band is broad and only Q1 is done; the mega deal transitions over a couple of months with steady state only by April 2027 and negligible FY27 revenue impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the AI datacenter investment look like a colocation-cost build (about $7M per MW), and what further commitments follow?
qa_highlights.answer: INR3,500 crore is only an initial fraction of the long-term 50 MW plan; it is a full-stack play, not colocation, with further investment tied to free cash flow and funded via partners, client commitments, hardware financing, and equity/debt mix.

qa_highlights.question: Token costs: will they collapse or stay high, and what does that mean for services revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said token prices may fall but total token consumption will rise, so total cost rises; tiered architecture with enterprise SLMs creates a new engineering services wave in data work and training.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to 18-19% soon, perhaps in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY26 margins were near 18% excluding restructuring; FY27 guidance is 17.5-18.5% including 40-50 bps restructuring; FY28 margin guidance will be given next year.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the ER&D decline and will it continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Decline was in Tech and Telecom and Media & Entertainment, from sharp discretionary cuts at two large US telcos flagged last quarter, plus a high base in tech; no explicit outlook for further declines was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter datacenters now, and how does this differ from the cloud cycle? Also, what about GPU oversupply risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued private AI stacks and SLMs differ from the cloud cycle, that megawatts are an anchor and value lies in wrapped services, and that the market remains GPU-starved; no explicit utilisation or tenancy assumptions were given.

qa_highlights.question: Does the margin guidance include amortization from M&A, and is the services outlook tougher than at the start of the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is organic and excludes acquisitions including Jaspersoft and CTG; macro view is unchanged since March and management will revisit after Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How big will Jaspersoft be, and when does CTG close?
qa_highlights.answer: Jaspersoft is expected to add about $10-15M per quarter with seasonality, consolidated from Q2; CTG expected to close later in Q2.

532281|2026-09.headline: HCLTech Q2 FY27 revenue rose 2.3% QoQ to $3,724M and EBIT margin hit 18.2%, while FY27 revenue guidance was narrowed to 2.5%-4%.
532281|2026-09.overview: Services grew 3% QoQ and 4% YoY in constant currency, led by Advanced AI revenue of $219M (up 28.4% QoQ, 78% YoY). New bookings were $3.3B (up 27% YoY, 35% QoQ), the second-highest quarter ever. HCLSoftware revenue fell 5.8% QoQ and 11.2% YoY to $294M, though ARR rose 7.8% YoY to $1.134B (2.6% ex-Jaspersoft). EBIT margin was 18.2%, up 131 bps QoQ, and FY27 EBIT guidance of 17.5%-18.5% was maintained.

Geographic growth YoY: USA +3.5%, Europe -0.3%, Rest of World +11.4%, India +21.8%. Retail and CPG +14% and Financial Services +7.1% led verticals; 5 of 7 verticals grew YoY.

qa_highlights.question: How is value shared between frontier AI labs and managed services, and how will it look in steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its value sits mainly in the FDE motion and services around OpenAI and Anthropic platforms, with a long tail of work once inside an enterprise. Pricing for some offerings includes token cost, making the economics non-linear rather than headcount-linked.

qa_highlights.question: Who is HCLTech competing with in Advanced AI deals?
qa_highlights.answer: The two largest AI deals were single-sourced via partners. Competition came from boutiques, and from service providers in agentic AI build, semiconductors and inferencing; IP platform monetization (e.g., AI Force line items) is now included in large deals.

qa_highlights.question: When will FCF-to-net-income conversion return to the 3-4 year average?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Shiv Walia said two one-time items (a bilateral advance pricing agreement tax payment and a contribution to an external gratuity trust) depressed LTM conversion; he expects it to revert to 100%+ as they roll out of LTM.

qa_highlights.question: Why not raise the top end of guidance given strong Services growth and a seasonally strong Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the environment remains volatile (citing the Middle East conflict) and it does not want to raise guidance; it expects Services slightly above the midpoint and a Q3 Software step-up.

qa_highlights.question: Are the AI engagements with OpenAI/Anthropic under T&M or fixed price, with meaningful TCV?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a mix: change management and operating model transformation engagements have some fixed-price deals, while agentic implementation on Google and similar platforms is largely time-and-materials.

qa_highlights.question: Are the ramp-downs in top-20 clients behind us?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact from the three ramp-downs was already in guidance, though discretionary spend at the two telco clients could still weigh. Upselling to existing clients has kept the client buckets growing.

qa_highlights.question: Why does Software margin expand while revenue declines, and how do Services margins look?
qa_highlights.answer: Software Q1 had a one-off restructuring cost; excluding it, lower employee costs and lower amortization drove the QoQ margin gain. Services margins benefited from Project Ascend and the higher Advanced AI mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the organic decline in Software and how long can ARR-to-revenue disconnect last?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue fell about 15% YoY on an organic basis while ARR rose 2.6% ex-Jaspersoft. Management attributed the gap to upfront recognition of multiyear licences and perpetual licence timing, expecting renewals to return in FY28 and FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Is there seasonality in HPE Telco Solutions (Aruba TS) revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only two months were consolidated and extrapolating to three months should be right; there may be small seasonality but nothing major.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q3-Q4 Services sequential growth expected to decelerate versus Q2 organic growth of about 2.4%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the mega deal not contributing until Q1 FY28 as the main outlier, and said it is being conservative given uncertainty, with Services likely above the midpoint.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue comes from ecosystem partners, and what is the impact of frontier-lab partnerships?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not track partner-channel revenue reliably, much of it is influenced rather than direct. It is a small but growing professional services partner for hyperscalers and frontier and GPU companies.

qa_highlights.question: What is the medium-term margin range?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said the earlier aspiration of 18%-19% remains the desired band, but he would not commit to it now, preferring to invest in capability and differentiation.

532285|2026-03.headline: Geojit's FY26 profit absorbed planned investments; distribution income up 10% and equity MF net inflow share rose to 0.40 from 0.33.
532285|2026-03.overview: Management framed FY26 as the first year of "Geojit 2.0", a shift toward recurring income (mutual fund distribution, advisory, PMS, insurance) with investments in sales headcount, IT and brand. Net sales headcount rose by about 700 to 3,768, including 650 in sales, at a cost of about INR29 crores, and brand spend rose by about INR15 crores. Profitability was hit by these investments, with about INR54 crores of transformation expenses booked and ROE reduced as brokerage income fell. Management said the next two years would carry similar investment costs, and it stopped field hiring for the current year because of the West Asia conflict.

qa_highlights.question: How is the DIFC entity traction, and how does it differ from the existing Middle East JVs? What is the NRI AUM?
qa_highlights.answer: DIFC is a private banking external-asset-manager business that started operations in February 2026, with client onboarding expected by end-May 2026. Existing Middle East entities are retail-focused. NRI AUM is INR12,000-13,000 crores, with about INR90 crores of income in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Hiring and capex plans for the current year?
qa_highlights.answer: Field hiring has been stopped because of the West Asia crisis; only replacements will be made. IT spend of about INR30 crores is planned over three years.

qa_highlights.question: Buyback plans and borrowing to fund MTF, given cash of about INR1,100 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed that borrowing is cheaper than using own cash and said it intends to borrow for MTF, LAS and NBFC needs. Buyback will be considered after SEBI rules are issued.

qa_highlights.question: Domestic client reaction in March and April?

532285|2026-06.headline: Geojit Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to INR160.4 crore and PAT to INR19.8 crore, but management guided to continued cost pressure and no hiring for several quarters.
532285|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR160.40 crore, up 11% YoY, with PBT of INR25.99 crore (up 4% QoQ) and PAT of INR19.83 crore (up 14% QoQ). Employee cost rose INR18 crore on sales force expansion, DIFC hiring, tech team additions and higher incentives, though management said employee cost would normalise after a lower insurance-incentive quarter. Customer assets reached INR1.11 lakh crore (up 15% QoQ), mostly from market appreciation, with recurring assets at INR26,000 crore. Management said margin benefits from FY26 investments would take a couple more quarters, and that hiring has been paused except for replacements due to Middle East conflict and market conditions. Leadership succession was also confirmed, with Jones George becoming MD from 1 October.

qa_highlights.answer: GCC AUM is a little under USD 1 billion. Middle East investment decisions are on hold, and no expansion is planned until stability returns.

532285|2026-09.headline: Geojit Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose 2.5% YoY to INR 165.82 crores, but cost growth and weak cash-market broking kept profitability subdued.
532285|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 165.82 crores, up 2.5% YoY and 3.38% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR 36.7 crores and PBT of INR 20.62 crores. H1 revenue rose 6.72% while H1 EBITDA was INR 78.23 crores, with management attributing the margin pressure to higher employee and technology costs alongside subdued cash-market transaction income. Recurring revenue AUM rose to INR 26,737 crores in H1 from INR 23,230 crores at end-FY26, and asset management AUM (PMS plus AIF) grew 39% from March to INR 2,018 crores. Customer assets were broadly flat at INR 1.12 lakh crores as market correction in September offset inflows.

financial_highlights.change: Margin declined YoY per analyst question; exact YoY not stated

vs INR 71 crores a year earlier; H1 INR 408 crores
Around INR 20,000 crores at end-August per management

financial_highlights.value: INR 156 crores monthly; about 1.78 lakh SIP clients

segments.name: Broking (cash and derivatives)
segments.commentary: Management said cash-market delivery volumes were subdued; derivatives are about 20% of total income and cash about 80%, of which about 90% is delivery. Transaction income is the main driver of EBITDA swings.

segments.commentary: Lending book of INR 780 crores, comprising margin trading facility and loan against shares and mutual funds.

segments.commentary: NRI business under pressure from FCNR deposit offers, rupee moves and GCC geopolitics; DIFC entity has about 50 relationships and about USD 2 million AUM booked, with revenue not yet meaningful.

NRI/GCC business faces wait-and-watch sentiment and FCNR competition; management reported no major redemption pressure.
ARR inflows were said to be broad-based rather than driven by large tickets; PMS average client size is about INR 75 lakhs.

qa_highlights.question: Were Q2 ARR inflows of INR 322 crores driven by a few large tickets or broad-based?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inflows were primarily broad-based, with a few high tickets. PMS average client size is about INR 75 lakhs on about INR 1,750 crores AUM.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the customer asset movement was MTM versus new inflows?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 inflows of about INR 1,400 crores equal only about 1.4% of INR 1 lakh crore base; the flat customer asset level mainly reflects market valuation changes.

qa_highlights.question: How will headcount and employee cost be managed?

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin improve and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin is tied to cash-market broking; management expects subdued margins for one to two quarters and cited historical 1-2 year lags before recovery.

532286|2026-03.headline: Jindal Steel Q4 FY26 consolidated adjusted EBITDA was INR 2,647 crores (INR 10,093/t) on ASP up INR 4,743/t QoQ, with FY27 sales guided at 10.5–11 Mt.
532286|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed a sharp sequential recovery: consolidated gross revenue rose 28% QoQ to INR 19,399 crores and adjusted EBITDA reached INR 2,647 crores, helped by a rise in HRC and TMT rebar prices and Angul volume ramp-up. Sales volume grew 15% QoQ to 2.62 Mt as the Angul expansion took steelmaking capacity to 15.6 Mtpa from 9.6 Mtpa. A one-time impairment of INR 1,433 crores (standalone) and INR 834 crores (consolidated) was booked on the Australian WCL asset after the shaft was closed. Management said the major capex programme is essentially complete and the focus shifts to asset sweating and deleveraging.

segments.name: Steel (India, Angul/Raigarh/Patratu)
segments.commentary: FY26 production 9.25 Mt (+14% YoY) and sales 8.68 Mt (+9% YoY). Q4 production 2.65 Mt (+6% QoQ, +26% YoY) and sales 2.62 Mt (+15% QoQ, +23% YoY). Flat/long mix was 52:48 in Q4 and 49:51 for FY26.

segments.name: Raw materials / overseas mines
segments.commentary: Iron ore sourcing about 60% outside purchases and 40% captive, with pricing described as stable. Mozambique is EBITDA positive, South Africa operating but not EBITDA positive, and Australia is closed with minimal cash burn.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: 1,050 MW Shree Bhoomi power plant commissioned (two 525 MW modules); ramp-up to complete within H1 FY27. Surplus power to be sold but described as not material to financials.

guidance_outlook: FY27 production guided at 11–11.5 Mt and sales at 10.5–11 Mt.
Q1 FY27 coking coal prices expected to rise by USD 20–25/t sequentially; iron ore movement of plus/minus INR 100–150/t per month.
Slurry pipeline (Barbil–Angul) to be commissioned in Q1 FY27; savings of about INR 700/t of iron ore, or INR 750–1,000/t of steel as it ramps up.
Port facility to be commissioned; DRI-2 (2 Mtpa) expected towards end of FY27; PP2 also remaining.
Capex guidance of INR 7,500–10,000 crores for expansion and sustenance capex; remaining programme capex INR 11,545 crores.
Leverage expected to normalise by Q2 FY27; value-added flat mix expected to move from about 50% toward 70%.
Start-up costs of INR 125 crores in Q4 are said to be finished and not recurring.
capex_capacity: Steelmaking capacity raised to 15.6 Mtpa from 9.6 Mtpa after BOF2 and BOF3 (3 Mt each) at Angul; iron-making capacity increased by 6.6 Mt through BF2 (4.6 Mt, operational) and DRI2 (2 Mt, under construction).
Cold rolling complex of 1.2 Mtpa commissioned at Angul to support value-added product mix.
Coal pipe conveyor from Utkal C thermal coal mine to Angul is operational; slurry pipeline from Barbil to Angul close to completion.
Total planned capex programme INR 47,043 crores: INR 25,924 crores spent up to FY25 and INR 9,574 crores in FY26, leaving INR 11,545 crores.
Thakurani-A1 iron ore block declared preferred bidder; Saradhapur Jalatap East coal block awarded at end of last year.
Rail rake programme of about 79 rakes: 72 acquired, remainder expected within 2–3 months.
demand_pricing: Management expects India steel demand growth of about 9–9.5% and cites FY26 finished steel consumption of 164.2 Mt (+8% YoY) and Q4 consumption of 44.6 Mt (+10% QoQ).

Realisations lag because the order book mixes spot and contract sales; contracts priced at earlier levels still support Q1 realisations. Management said the market is holding firm despite a slight dip in recent weeks.
Management declined to give a Q1/Q2 realisation upside estimate, saying the market is hard to predict.
Flat sales focus is on infrastructure first, then building and construction, downstream products and automobiles. HSM grades developed for niche products are ramping in the current quarter.
Management said the Q4 sales run rate reflects seasonality, so no large sequential volume pickup is expected.
Safeguard duty on flat steel imports reduced to 11.5% from 12% effective 21 Apr 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Will steel and realisation gains continue into Q1, and have contracts been reset?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contracts on earlier prices continue and ASP rose strongly in Q4 because of the spot/contract lag; the market is holding firm, though slightly softer recently.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company shift to asset sweating rather than further capacity expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed the capex programme is essentially complete and the focus is on sweating assets, with INR 7,500–10,000 crores allocated to expansion and sustenance capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why is value-added share falling and what is the target mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the priority during ramp-up is utilisation, with mix optimisation starting in H1 FY27 and stabilising in H2. Flat mix is about 50:50 today and is expected to reach about 70% flat over time.

qa_highlights.question: What were the start-up costs this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put Q4 start-up costs at INR 125 crores, most of which were booked in Q3, and said these will not recur.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the slurry pipeline savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said slurry savings are about INR 700/t of iron ore, or INR 750–1,000/t of steel as it ramps. Full utilisation is not expected this year, but per-tonne savings do not depend on utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further write-downs on overseas assets?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said no further write-downs are expected, based on an independent valuation. Australia has minimal cash outflow, and Mozambique is EBITDA positive.

qa_highlights.question: What are the raw material cost moves into Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Coking coal is expected to rise USD 20–25/t QoQ in Q1. Iron ore is expected to move by about plus/minus INR 100–150/t per month and is hard to predict.

risks_watch: Value-added product share fell to about 61% from 66% QoQ, and management says mix will move back toward normal levels only over time.
Coking coal cost increase of USD 20–25/t in Q1 FY27 could compress margins if steel prices soften; a dip in steel prices was acknowledged.
FY26 EBITDA per tonne fell to INR 10,482 from INR 11,712 in FY25 even as volume rose.
DRI-2 is due towards end FY27 and PP2 is also pending; slurry pipeline commissioning is due in Q1 FY27.

Overseas mine EC capacity increase is pending with no date given.

532286|2026-06.headline: Jindal Steel Q1FY27 consolidated adjusted EBITDA INR 2,667 crore, INR 11,937/ton, with ASP up INR 7,500/ton despite 15% sequential volume drop.
532286|2026-06.overview: Q1FY27 revenue fell about 8% QoQ on a plant maintenance shutdown (BOF refractory change), with sales volume down 15% sequentially. ASP rose about INR 7,500/ton on stronger steel prices and richer mix, and value-added share rose from 61% to 66%. Adjusted EBITDA was INR 2,667 crore (INR 11,937/ton, up INR 1,843/ton), while PAT was INR 844 crore and finance cost rose to INR 548 crore as Q4FY26 expansion assets entered the P&L. Management guided to net debt/EBITDA below 1.5x in Q2FY27 (Q1: 1.71x) and a sequential cost recovery from the shutdown reversing, with the slurry pipeline targeted for commissioning around August.

532286|2026-09.headline: Jindal Steel posted record Q2 FY27 gross revenue of INR 19,448 crore (+44% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of INR 2,504 crore (+34% YoY) on 2.38 MT sales.

Adjusted EBITDA rose 34% YoY to INR 2,504 crore, but adjusted EBITDA per ton of INR 10,529 was sequentially lower on higher raw material, power, fuel and freight costs. Net debt fell to INR 14,786 crore and net debt-to-EBITDA improved to 1.51x from 1.71x. Management guided to 11 MT gross steel output in FY27 with H2 net steel of about 6 MT, and said the switch from propane to coal-gas syngas protected productivity during the West Asia supply disruption.

qa_highlights.question: How much more US litigation charge visibility is there after H1 provisions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most big cases are settled; only small amounts are expected going forward, over quarters and years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Flovent headroom and Monroe filing timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Flovent 44 is the sole generic and performing as expected; fluticasone nasal spray commercialisation is starting, with Flovent 110 and ipratropium launches toward year-end. Three to four Monroe injectable products expected next year.

qa_highlights.question: How will EBITDA margin trajectory look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets a YoY percentage margin improvement, with H2 benefits from the front-loaded H1 field force and oncology investments; oncology products expected to lift margins from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why was H1 operating cash flow negative?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR520 crore of litigation payments, INR337 crore capex, plus interest, dividends and working capital; H2 cash generation expected at INR400-800 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gross and net debt at end-September?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt about INR866.5 crore and cash INR1,290 crore, giving net cash of INR424 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margin expectations for the oncology products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA will be well ahead of the company average, around 30-40% net margin for the oncology products.

risks_watch: H1 operating cash flow negative; H2 must deliver INR400-800 crore to reach zero gross debt and INR1,200 crore cash by year-end.
Residual US litigation settlements may continue over quarters and years.
European generics expected to grow only low single digit; CEE demand softer.
Geopolitical and supply chain cost pressure across the value chain, per management.
ISB 2001 licensing outside AbbVie's territories not discussed; STAR-0310 rights returned from BioCryst effective 4 November, with partnering under evaluation.
532296|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and H2 operating leverage, but guarded on specifics: management declined to share ISB 2001 ASH data or licensing plans and gave no quantified EBITDA margin target beyond a YoY improvement.
key_quotes: Excluding the various one-offs from the last year, as well as looking at our core business P&L, excluding IGI, we delivered a 20% Y-o-Y growth in revenue, along with 21% EBITDA margin in Q2.
As the operating leverage kicks in in H2 FY 2027, we expect gross debt to be zero by end of FY 2027.
I think most of our big cases have been settled, right? Now, going forward, we anticipate there will be some possible small amounts which will go out as we go forward.

532300|2026-03.headline: Wockhardt FY26 revenue INR3,373 crore, EBITDA about INR630 crore (~51% growth); Zaynich US FDA approval is the key catalyst, with peak sales guided at $1.5-2 billion globally.
532300|2026-03.overview: Management hosted an investor meet on 4 June 2026 (disclosed 11 June) after the US FDA approval of Zaynich (cefepime-zidebactam), described as the first Indian-discovered research product approved by the FDA. FY26 revenue was INR3,373 crore, EBITDA about INR630 crore (margin about 18.6%, up from about 5.4% three years earlier) and profit before tax INR238 crore. Management framed the next phase as scaling growth: US launch of Zaynich via an operationally light model, India and emerging-market launches, and biosimilar diabetes expansion. Most numbers were given verbally; no quarterly figures or formal guidance were disclosed in the presentation.

segments.name: Pharma core (India, UK, Ireland)
segments.commentary: About 75% of business; UK is top-five with 18% covered-market share and focuses on specialty injectables. India driven by diabetes, orthopedics, pain and regenerative medicine (Emrok, Miqnaf).

segments.name: Biosimilars / biotech (diabetes)
segments.commentary: Grew 27% in FY26; human insulin output scaled 2x and glargine 1.5x. Two products commercialised, five in pipeline (aspart, RN 30/70, degludec, degludec aspart, semaglutide); registered in 30 emerging markets.

segments.name: Novel antibiotics (Zaynich, Emrok, Miqnaf, Odrate)
segments.commentary: Specialty (biosimilars plus novel antibiotics) is 23% of business. Zaynich has US FDA and CDSCO India approvals; US launch planned with leadership hired and a commercial operating partner; European approval expected by end of calendar 2026.

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.commentary: 28% of turnover, growing 35%, supported by partnerships in Brazil, Thailand, Algeria and Malaysia. Plans to launch Zaynich in seven to eight high-carbapenem-resistance markets within 18 to 24 months.

guidance_outlook: Zaynich global peak sales of $1.5-2 billion per year, with US roughly 40% of global revenue; country-wise split not given.
Revenue ramp expected to be slow initially (hockey-stick pattern), with breakeven in 12 to 18 months in the Zaynich business; first 12-18 months may see a slight loss, per the Chairman.
Zaynich US price expected at roughly $1,200-1,500 per day, with India pricing about 75-80% below US; Europe and US pricing described as price-neutral versus existing antibiotics.
Long-term target of about 20-25% share of resistant cases globally; India possibly higher.
Biosimilar business expected to double in 24-36 months; capacity to double in 12-15 months; five pipeline products to launch about two years out.
Capex of INR200-300 crore over next three years, primarily for biologicals capacity; R&D spend to stay at similar percentage of sales.
Foviscu DCGI filing expected in two to three months; approval timing not predictable. Odrate is about four years away and Phase 2 waiver not expected.
capex_capacity: Planned capex of INR200-300 crore over the next three years, mainly for biologicals capacity.
Biosimilar capacity to double within 12-15 months.

Zaynich manufacturing: US supply from an FDA-approved European site; India supply from Indian facility; emerging markets to be supplied from either India or Europe depending on timelines (Europe could save six to nine months).
Company has 11 manufacturing facilities and two R&D centres in-house.
Management said US, Europe and emerging markets filings are submitted or in progress, with European approval expected by end of 2026.
demand_pricing: US cUTI is the largest of about 1.2 million US gram-negative hospital infections (about 600,000 cUTI cases); management cited about 20-25% readmission rate for cUTI.
India: about 600,000-700,000 gram-negative infection patients, with 35-45% estimated carbapenem resistance (ICMR surveillance caveated by regional variation).
Phase 3 vs meropenem: composite cure rate 96.8%, about 20% higher than meropenem per management.
Management said new anti-infectives in the US market total about $1 billion; the company does not plan to create new demand but to take share, with price neutrality.
Competition: cefiderocol (Fetroja) cited as the closest competitor; management claimed Zaynich has a better efficacy and safety profile, without numerical head-to-head data.

qa_highlights.question: Expected revenue from Zaynich over the next 6 to 24 months, and capex and commercial costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman expects slow initial revenue growth, a hockey-stick curve after 12-18 months, INR200-300 crore capex over three years, and no capex for sales build-out, only revenue cost. Breakeven expected in 12-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Does Zaynich qualify for the 10% PLI and what is the China strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Government funding recognised but immaterial versus R&D spend. China: Chinese patients in trial were insufficient; a small China study is ongoing and a partner may be sought.

qa_highlights.question: Will Zaynich be made in Europe for the US and in India for emerging markets?
qa_highlights.answer: US supply from an FDA-inspected European site as a de-risking step; India supply from India; emerging markets from India or Europe depending on timelines.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Wockhardt exit US generics and will it re-enter?
qa_highlights.answer: US generics were about 5% of the portfolio and loss-making, amid the 2012-13 FDA import alert. Management said it is re-entering with innovative products sourced from European manufacturers, with India production for India.

qa_highlights.question: Patent life and exclusivity for Zaynich, Emrok and Miqnaf?
qa_highlights.answer: Zaynich patent runs to 2038 in India with further filings planned; Miqnaf patent to early 2033 in India. QIDP status gives five extra years in US; minimum 10-year market exclusivity in US and Western markets.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing and patient targets for FY28-FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: US price about $1,200-1,500 per day, typically $10,000-15,000 per course; India priced about 75-80% below US. Long-term share of 20-25% of resistant cases, with no FY28-29 patient numbers given.

qa_highlights.question: Peak sales of Zaynich?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said $1.5-2 billion per year globally at peak, not cumulative, with US around 40% of global revenue.

risks_watch: Commercial execution: a new US sales model for antibiotics with a commercial operating partner, 6,000 US hospitals to segment, and a first-time anti-infective launch for the company.
Losses or breakeven in the first 12-18 months from US launch costs; Chairman's comments on profitability were clarified as Zaynich-only.
Regulatory timing: European approval expected by end-2026, emerging market filings to follow; DCGI approval for Foviscu not predictable.
Label scope: US approval is for cUTI; HAP/VAP and other indications need a further trial, so off-label use is a question.
Zaynich Phase 2 waiver for the aztreonam combination (Odrate) not expected; Odrate timing about four years.
Hospital segment profitability and ROCE targets were not answered (hospitals deemed out of scope; ROCE question deflected).
532300|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and promotional on Zaynich and the R&D pipeline, with forward-looking claims (peak sales, market share) given without detailed assumptions. Evasive or deflective on ROCE, hospitals, Foviscu timing and China specifics, and on country-wise revenue split.
key_quotes: Wockhardt, as you know, in the last few days, is now the first Indian company to have an Indian research product approved with the US FDA, Zaynich.
So, it is in your financial terms you say investment, I mean, asset-light and capital-heavy.
We will stick to only antibiotic research for next 10 years.
Peak sales per year.

rows.why: Capex of INR200-300 crore over three years, mainly biologicals, is already firmly planned; utilisation was not disclosed, so further capex beyond this is not signalled.

rows.why: Zaynich has US FDA and CDSCO approvals with leadership hired and a commercial partner in place; European approval is expected by end of calendar 2026, and emerging-market launches in seven to eight markets are planned within 18-24 months.

rows.label: Zaynich emerging-market launches in 7-8 high-CRE markets
rows.why: Management plans launches in seven to eight high carbapenem-resistance markets, with emerging markets already 28% of turnover growing 35% and partnerships in Brazil, Thailand, Algeria and Malaysia.

rows.when: filing in 2-3 months; approval timing unpredictable
rows.why: Filing is expected in two to three months, but management would not predict approval timing, so this is a binary timing risk.

532305|2026-06.headline: Ind-Swift Q1 FY27 operating EBITDA rose 2.85x YoY to ₹33.32 crore, a 17.91% margin, with management guiding to 20%+ from Q3.
532305|2026-06.overview: Operating income grew 21.16% YoY to ₹186.08 crore and operating EBITDA reached ₹33.32 crore (17.91% margin, up 1258 bps). PAT excluding exceptional items was ₹24.68 crore (13.26% margin vs 4.99%). Management attributed the step-up to exit of litigation and other costs borne by the formulation business after the merger, and to a higher own-brand export mix. CDMO contracts with Viatris, Manx and Arrotex were commercialised in the quarter but contributed only about ₹5-6 crore so far, with ramp-up expected from Q2 and Q3. Management reiterated FY27 export sales of about ₹750 crore and ₹1200 crore revenue by FY29, and declined to revise targets at this stage.

segments.name: Export own-brands
segments.commentary: 57.20% of Q1 FY27 sales versus 48% in Q1 FY26; management cites this mix shift as a key margin driver. Export gross margin was stated at about 55%.

segments.name: Export contract manufacturing (CDMO)
segments.commentary: 26.64% of Q1 FY27 sales versus 29% a year earlier. Viatris, Manx and Arrotex partnerships commercialised in the quarter, with about ₹5-6 crore booked from Viatris products (Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules) so far.

segments.name: Domestic segments
segments.commentary: Branded generics 6.41%, ethical 6.14% and domestic contract manufacturing 3.61% of Q1 FY27 sales, all lower than a year ago. Management describes these as a stable cash-generation base; domestic sales are seasonal.

segments.name: Product portfolio
segments.commentary: Ezetimibe + Atorvastatin was about ₹25 crore in Q1 FY27 per management, partnered with Tiffen-Becker. FY26 revenue: Atorvastatin ₹85.50 crore, Ezetimibe + Atorvastatin ₹80.78 crore, Fexofenadine ₹74.32 crore, Quetiapine ₹19.75 crore, Famciclovir ₹18.64 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 export sales target of about ₹750 crore, with roughly 45% from CDMO (per management).

FY29 revenue target of ₹1200 crore; management said it is not revising this yet and will revisit by year-end. Mentioned FY27 expectation of about ₹900 crore and a longer-term aspiration of ₹1500 crore revenue and ~₹200 crore net profit by FY30.
EBITDA margin of 18% described as sustainable; management expects to move above 20% from Q3 FY27 (Q2 internally targeted), potentially 21-22% with sequential sales growth.
Viatris CDMO volumes expected to double in Q2 versus Q1; Arrotex Macrogol push expected in Q2, and Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules to contribute in Q3-Q4.
Medium-term growth of 20-25% CAGR referenced, with EBITDA margins above 18% (management answered 'yes').
Dossiers to reach 400+ additions, taking the total from 2,100 to about 2,500 by Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: About ₹250 crore of cash to be deployed in capex over roughly 2 to 2.5 years across a new warehouse, capacity enhancement at the existing facility, and the Jammu facility (EU-GMP/PIC/S audit under way).
Samba facility upgrade to EU-GMP and PIC/S standards in progress as planned.
Capacity utilisation for Ibuprofen and granules about 70% in Q1 per management; management expects 90% utilisation of planned FY29 capacity over time.
Capex for a potential new CDMO customer deal estimated at ₹50-75 crore, with revenue of ₹150+ crore expected.
R&D working on 5-6 molecules for FY27-29; capex to follow only after filings are completed. New R&D land bought in Panchkula area.
demand_pricing: CDMO economics: Viatris paid about USD 2 million for development work, to be reimbursed through orders.
Selection criteria for new products include a minimum 50-55% gross margin and customer confidence in R&D delivery. Candidate molecules include Rosuvastatin, Mirabegron, Sitagliptin and Empagliflozin.
Tiffen-Becker arrangement: transfer-priced supply with about 43% of the customer's margin shared with Ind-Swift.
Management expects no dearth of capacity for the planned growth; new partnerships under discussion with 3-4 existing overseas customers, not expected to contribute this year.

qa_highlights.question: What was the CDMO contribution in Q1 and what growth to expect from the Viatris partnership over three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Gagan Aggarwal said Viatris products (Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules) booked only about ₹5-6 crore in Q1, with growth reflecting in Q2 and Q3. He said about ₹100-130 crore is expected from these two products, not the full ₹200 crore in year one, and that it would build over about two years.

qa_highlights.question: What are export margins for CDMO and own-brands, and how will the ₹250 crore cash and Synthimed stake be used?
qa_highlights.answer: Export gross margin is about 55%. The ₹250 crore cash will be deployed as capex over about 2.5 years (warehouse, existing capacity, Jammu). No plans to divest the Synthimed stake this year; Synthimed budgeted EBITDA is about ₹750 crore and Q1 results are on track.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 18% EBITDA margin sustainable, and could it rise further?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 18% is fully sustainable and could reach 21-22% if sales grow quarter on quarter. It denied calling Q1 a turnaround, citing litigation and other costs borne by the formulation business for about 1.5 years that are now over.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY29 revenue guidance of ₹1200 crore not being raised, and when does growth come?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will not revise at this stage and will revisit by year-end. Growth is H2-weighted via Arrotex Macrogol in Q2 and Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules in Q3-Q4. FY27 expectation is about ₹900 crore, with export sales of about ₹750 crore, roughly 45% from CDMO.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the API business sold and what R&D capability was retained?
qa_highlights.answer: The API business was sold to Synthimed in FY24 for net about ₹2000-2100 crore, used to repay group debt of about ₹1250-1300 crore. Retained R&D in Panchkula handles regulatory compliance, tech transfer and global filings, with new land bought for a further R&D facility.

qa_highlights.question: What is capacity utilisation and will there be a capacity shortfall?
qa_highlights.answer: Ibuprofen and granules ran at about 70% in Q1 on pilot batches. Management expects 90% utilisation of the FY29 plan over time and sees no capacity dearth. Capex for new molecules will follow only after filings are complete.

risks_watch: CDMO ramp-up timing: Viatris volumes are guided to double in Q2 from a ₹5-6 crore base, and Arrotex Macrogol and Ibuprofen and granules contributions depend on Q2-Q4 execution.
Margin trajectory: management targets above 20% EBITDA margin from Q3 FY27 (Q2 internally), against 17.91% in Q1; a shortfall would challenge the 21-22% view.
Capacity and capex: ₹250 crore capex over about 2-2.5 years, Jammu and Samba EU-GMP/PIC/S audits in progress, and the new CDMO deal needs ₹50-75 crore capex; delays could cap FY28-29 revenue.
Revenue guidance: FY27 about ₹900 crore and FY29 ₹1200 crore; management says it will revisit by year-end, so the next quarter's run-rate matters.
Synthimed stake: ~7.8% holding, no divestment planned this year, tag-along right on any PE exit; monetisation timing is open.
Customer concentration and unnamed partners: two new overseas CDMO deals and 3-4 existing customers are under discussion but not named; 'the war' is cited as slowing signings.
Several questions were deferred (market size, Q1 capacity utilisation, new registrations, packaging differentiation), so follow-ups via IR are pending.
key_quotes: Yes, yes, 18% is fully sustainable and we plan if the sales we are able to increase quarter-on-quarter they might go up to 21 to 22%.
Sir, not at this stage. Maybe after if we are able to achieve our, overachieve our results this financial year, we may revise this.

We don't want to spend a single penny in R&D before we sign off any agreement with our customers.

Evasive on several detailed questions, including market size, Q1 capacity utilisation, partner names and new registrations, which were deferred to follow-up.

rows.why: Viatris volumes guided to double in Q2 from ₹5-6 cr booked in Q1, with Viatris CDMO expected to contribute ~₹100-130 cr over about two years.

532305|2026-09.headline: Ind-Swift Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 50.15% YoY to ₹234.89 crore, with operating EBITDA margin at 18.02% and PAT of ₹31.03 crore.
532305|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 operating revenue was ₹234.89 crore, up 50.15% YoY and 26.22% QoQ, with operating EBITDA of ₹42.33 crore (18.02% margin) and PAT of ₹31.03 crore (13.21% margin). H1 FY27 revenue reached ₹420.97 crore (up 35.79% YoY), with H1 EBITDA margin at 17.97%. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth guidance of more than 50% and a medium-term target of ₹1,500+ crore by FY30, but did not commit to a 20% full-year EBITDA margin, which management called an internal target. Several questions on constant-currency figures, detailed capex and FY28 guidance were deferred or left open.

4.95x YoY from ₹8.55 crore; +27.04% QoQ from ₹33.32 crore

Samba plant utilisation at 70-75%; Derabassi (100% EOU) utilisation at 70-75%.

Derabassi warehouse land acquired, construction started; warehouse shift expected in 10-12 months, freeing space for additional manufacturing. Management said Derabassi capacity is sufficient to reach ₹1,200 crore by FY28.
Samba: ANVISA (Brazil) visit expected probably in Q4 FY27; PIC/S/EU approval expected sometime in FY28.

Macrogol sachet (Aerotex): product developed in-house and supplied.

Europe is about 47% of geographic export mix; management said Europe is stable and payment-oriented, so no reduction is planned.
NPPA revised price control list: no impact, as the portfolio falls outside it.
New-customer revenue of about ₹80-90 crore this year from newly acquired international customers.

qa_highlights.question: Sourcing of APIs and key starting materials?

qa_highlights.question: Pipeline and new molecule timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: There are 11 molecules due by FY28-FY29 and two more in FY29-FY30. Management said no new molecule is expected in FY28. Products are finished formulations, not APIs. Registrations start in early FY28; commercialisation late FY28 or FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and receivables?

532309|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 PBT from continuing operations hit INR 119 crore, but one-offs (incl. ~INR 44 crore BHEL ECL reversal) drove much of it; underlying FY26 EBITDA margin 11%.
532309|2026-03.overview: GE Power India reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR 316 crore (up from INR 266 crore YoY) and FY26 revenue of INR 1,269 crore (up 21%), led by Core Services (+14%) and Upgrades (+24%). Profit before tax and exceptional items from continuing operations was INR 119 crore in Q4 versus a loss of INR 15 crore a year earlier, and INR 340 crore for FY26 versus INR 22 crore, with management flagging sizeable one-offs in both periods. Order intake fell sharply to INR 877 crore for FY26 from INR 2,183 crore, and order backlog declined to INR 1,628 crore from INR 2,662 crore, mainly due to termination of FGD-EP contracts. Management is pushing a service-led, short-cycle strategy, has settled with BHEL and Jaypee, and has signed a Durgapur demerger to JSW Energy, with a recommended dividend of INR 7 per share (70% of face value).

segments.name: Core Services
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew 14% YoY and core orders rose 32% YoY; Core Services order backlog up about 40% YoY. Management says about 85-90% of the 31 Mar 2026 order book executes in FY27 (12-month cycles).

segments.name: Upgrades
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew 24% YoY, driven by upgrade volumes in Q4; Vindhyachal and Wanakbori complex upgrade orders of INR 591 crore were booked in FY25.

segments.name: New Build / FGD EPC (AQCS)
segments.commentary: In close-out mode; FGD-EP contracts of Jaypee Bina and Nigrie (INR 775 crore) were terminated, driving backlog decline. Seven operational acceptances and four unit completions achieved in FY26.

segments.name: Durgapur manufacturing (discontinued)
segments.commentary: Being demerged to JSW Energy; asset of about 660 acres, reported losses in recent quarters. Five-year JSW supply and capacity agreement signed to protect core services manufacturing needs.

guidance_outlook: Management did not give numeric FY27 guidance; CFO said the FY26 underlying EBITDA base (11%) is set and FY27 margins should be at par or better, without a range.
About 85-90% of the 31 Mar 2026 order book (INR 1,628 crore) expected to execute in FY27, implying roughly INR 1,380-1,470 crore; this is a management estimate from the call, not formal guidance.
Durgapur demerger to JSW Energy: filed with NCLT; target completion in calendar 2026, and within 12 months of 31 Mar 2026 at the latest.
Core Services target addressable fleet of about INR 3,500-4,000 crore; company holds about 18% share and aims to grow it before considering other areas.
Management says the ECL impact from the BHEL settlement is fully recognised as of 31 Mar 2026, so no similar reversal is expected in FY27.
capex_capacity: Durgapur manufacturing facility to be demerged to JSW Energy; a five-year agreement with JSW covers reserved manufacturing capacity and supply for core services boiler components.
Management aims to build an alternate supply chain for boiler components within about 18 months to become independent of JSW after the five-year agreement.
Three PG tests completed for key new-build units and multiple synchronisations and facility closures achieved in FY26.
Eighteen new first-of-its-kind service products ordered during FY26; first-time generator repairs, turbine upgrades and control system solutions delivered.
demand_pricing: Management says thermal plant PLF and availability are rising, increasing services demand; target addressable market quoted at INR 3,500-4,000 crore.
Q4 order intake of INR 254 crore was below the prior-year INR 285 crore (which included INR 52 crore O&M); FY26 orders fell 60% YoY on the FY25 FGD-EP and complex upgrade wins.

FGD mandate: per the July 2025 notification, Category C plants (over 200 GW) were removed and Category A (about 8 GW, mainly Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra) must install FGD; Category B is optional with no tariff pass-through if they opt in. Management says the mandate has limited near-term order impact.
Management is pursuing 13 countries for boilers, including Vietnam, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Indonesia, while stating its perimeter remains India-only for GEPIL and non-GEPIL assets.

qa_highlights.question: Does GEPIL participate in gas turbine, HRSG or combined-cycle business?
qa_highlights.answer: Puneet Bhatla said no; HRSG and gas-plant business belong to GE Vernova's gas business and fall outside GEPIL's objects, which are steam and thermal only.

qa_highlights.question: Of the order book, how much is executable in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Aashish Ghai said short-cycle orders typically complete within 12 months, so about 85-90% of the 31 Mar 2026 order book is expected in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will backlog grow after the current book runs off, and is the business widening beyond core?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline is new-build close-out. Core backlog is up about 40% YoY; the company plans to grow its 18% share of the INR 3,500-4,000 crore fleet before expanding to other areas.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 450 crore loan and what yield does it earn?
qa_highlights.answer: Ghai said it is surplus cash lent to a promoter-group cash pool benchmarked to HSBC, with rates of 5.5-6.35% in FY26, about 0.25% above commercial bank deposit rates. Lending is board-approved, shareholder-approved and audited.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scope of the FGD opportunity and the margin range?
qa_highlights.answer: Roshan Singh outlined the notification: Category A (about 8 GW) must install FGD, Category B is optional, and Category C was removed. He said the mandate has limited weight for GEPIL unless utilities act proactively. No margin range was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the INR 880 crore net cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Puneet Bhatla said the cash is under evaluation for deployment into growth in services, with no specific plan disclosed yet and shareholder value as the stated priority.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Durgapur demerger timeline and benefit to minority shareholders?
qa_highlights.answer: Ghai said the NCLT petition is filed, creditor and shareholder approvals and tax/bank NOCs are required, and completion is targeted for this calendar year and within 12 months of 31 Mar 2026. Shareholders receive entitlement shares in the resulting company.

qa_highlights.question: Will the demerger affect manufacturing needed for core services?
qa_highlights.answer: Ghai said no, because a five-year JSW Energy agreement reserves manufacturing capacity at pre-set schedule and price. An alternate supply chain is targeted within about 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the underlying EBITDA margin excluding one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Ghai said FY26 normalised entity-level EBITDA was 11%, with Q4 at about 18%. He declined to give a numeric margin range for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will ECL-related reversals continue in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Ghai said no; the BHEL settlement is fully executed, with the final tranche received in March 2026, and the ECL impact is complete as of 31 Mar 2026.

532321|2026-03.headline: Zydus Q4 FY26 revenue up 16% YoY to ₹75.9bn with EBITDA margin at 33.7%; FY27 guided to high-teens consolidated growth and >24% margin.
532321|2026-03.overview: Zydus closed FY26 with consolidated revenue of ₹271.5bn (up 17%) and EBITDA of ₹84.8bn (up 20%), with a record 31.2% full-year EBITDA margin. Q4 revenue of ₹75.9bn rose 16% YoY and 11% QoQ, with EBITDA margin of 33.7%, helped by product mix, operating leverage and forex. The company made several acquisitions (Comfort Click, Amplitude Surgical, LiqMeds) and proposed the Assertio Holdings deal for US specialty oncology, while net debt/EBITDA was 0.5x at March 2026. Management guided FY27 to high-teens revenue growth and EBITDA margin above 24%, with US growth in single digits on a high base.

532331|2026-09.headline: Ajanta Q2 FY27 revenue rose 33% to Rs 1,794 crore and PAT 49% to Rs 388 crore, but management guided to a weaker H2 on US and institutional normalisation.
532331|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 33% to Rs 1,794 crore, EBITDA rose 47% to Rs 543 crore (30% margin) and PAT rose 49% to Rs 388 crore. Every business grew in the quarter, led by US generics (+41%), Africa branded generics (+41%) and Africa Institution (+259%), with Asia branded generics rebounding 18%. Management said H1 benefited from elevated US sales on a limited-competition product and an unusually strong institutional quarter, both of which will normalise in H2. FY27 guidance was retained at high-teens revenue growth, around 27% EBITDA margin and around 78% gross margin, with US growth guidance cut to high single digits from mid single digits.

532343|2026-03.headline: TVS Motor FY26 revenue rose 30% to INR 47,270 crores with record Q4 revenue of INR 12,808 crores and 13.1% EBITDA margin.
532343|2026-03.overview: TVS Motor reported record FY26 volume of 5.9 million units (up 24%), revenue of INR 47,270 crores (up 30%) and operating PBT of INR 4,975 crores (up 40%). Q4 revenue of INR 12,808 crores grew 36% YoY with EBITDA margin of 13.1%, against 6.5% when the margin recovery began. Management flagged near-term supply disruptions (gas, labour at Tier 2 suppliers, raw material timing, container lead times) and 3-5% commodity cost inflation, and guided to a strong single-digit industry growth in FY27 with capex of about INR 3,500 crores.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA up 37% from INR 4,450 crores; margin up 60 bps from 12.3%
vs INR 1,172 crores in Q4 FY25
vs INR 851 crores in Q4 FY25
PBT up 22%; book up 15% from INR 26,647 crores

segments.name: 2-wheeler ICE (domestic)
segments.commentary: FY26 2W ICE sales grew 22% vs industry 12%; Q4 domestic ICE grew 26% vs industry 24%. Scooter category share is about 38% (including EV), which management expects to exceed 40%.

segments.name: Electric 2-wheeler
segments.commentary: FY26 EV 2W sales of 3.7 lakh units, up 33% from 2.8 lakh; Q4 EV sales 115,000, up 51%. EV penetration rose to 6.6% for FY26 (6.2% prior) and 7.8% in Q4 (7.1% prior). FY26 EV revenue about INR 5,000 crores.

segments.name: 3-wheeler
segments.commentary: FY26 sales 220,000 units, up 63% from 135,000; Q4 60,000 units, up 65% from 37,000.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Record FY26 international sales of 15.8 lakh units, up 33%; Q4 international revenue INR 2,999 crores. Q4 international sales grew 23%. Spare parts revenue in Q4 about INR 1,122 crores.

segments.name: TVS Credit
segments.commentary: FY26 PBT INR 1,248 crores (up 22%); Q4 PBT INR 348 crores (up 15%). Added about 53 lakh new customers, total base about 2.4 crore; rated AA+.

segments.name: Norton (overseas subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Majority of the roughly INR 2,400 crores FY26 investment went to Norton; new models Manx, Manx R, Atlas and Atlas GT to be launched with Q2 FY27 as a key milestone. Some models to be built at Solihull and others at Hosur.

guidance_outlook: FY27 domestic industry growth guided at a strong single digit; TVS aims to grow ahead of the industry in both domestic and international markets.
Q1 FY27 expected to show very good growth ahead of the industry in both retail and dispatches, as supply constraints ease in May and are expected to clear by end-May or early June.
FY27 capex expected at about INR 3,500 crores: about INR 2,000 crores on product development, over INR 1,000 crores on 1.5 million unit capacity addition, and higher R&D spend.
Overseas investment in FY27 expected to be about 70% of FY26 level (INR 500-600 crores lower than INR 2,400 crores), though not zero.

Management declined to give margin guidance; said cost inflation of 3-5% of revenue is significant, with about 35% offset so far through price increases, and cited mix, scale and cost reduction as offsets.
Management expects 2W EV and scooter segments to grow well in FY27; the economy segment is expected to face challenges.
capex_capacity: Immediate plan to add about 1.5 million units of capacity, taking total to about 8.3 million units; work started in Q4 FY26 and the first significant addition in 12 months.
Capacity planning for FY28-29 under review quarter by quarter; aim is for capacity not to constrain growth.
EV production currently averages around 40,000 units/month (FY26 average 30,000-32,000), with a target of 50,000 per month soon.
Norton products in development at Hosur and Solihull; new Norton models expected in Q2 FY27.
Overseas: Dubai strategic investment about INR 300 crores made; TVS Credit investment about INR 200 crores in FY26.
demand_pricing: Demand described as strong across domestic and international for all models, but supply was the binding constraint. Dealer inventory is kept at 21-30 days and is being rebuilt; channel stock is expected to normalise by end-May or early June.
Commodity cost inflation (steel, aluminium, crude derivatives, gas) estimated at 3-5% of revenue; about 35% offset through price increases so far.
PLI incentive income for Q4 was about 0.9% of revenue.
Ronin monthly domestic volume crossed 8,000 units; management targets above 10,000. Indonesia averaged about 20,000 units per month, up from 17,000.
Africa and Asia are core; LatAm is a multi-year focus. International container lead times rose about 15% (around 8-10 days) amid geopolitical disruption.
3-wheeler: VAHAN share of EV 3W rising; new launches include King Kargo EV and King Kargo Heavy Duty CNG cargo; Hyundai JDA signed to co-develop an EV 3W.

qa_highlights.question: What growth is expected in FY27 for domestic and international, and how will segments perform?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects strong single-digit industry growth, with scooters, EVs and premium/super-premium growing well and the economy segment facing headwinds. TVS expects to outgrow the industry.

qa_highlights.question: What commodity inflation and price increases are expected in Q1 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Commodity inflation is about 3-5% of revenue, with about 35% offset by price increases so far. Mix, scale and cost reduction are the other levers.

qa_highlights.question: What are current 2W and 3W production capacities and the planned additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is being increased by 1.5 million units to about 8.3 million. Management said this is the first significant addition in 12 months, and capacity will not constrain growth.

qa_highlights.question: Where are supply-chain constraints (raw materials, labour, rare earths) and channel stock?
qa_highlights.answer: Constraints are energy/gas, Tier 2 labour shortages and raw material timing. May is better than April, and channel stock should normalise by end-May or early June. Q4 international revenue was INR 2,999 crores and spare parts INR 1,122 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why is management cautious for the next two quarters, and what are the risks to demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand is strong and the uncertainty is on raw material timing and Tier 2 disruption, which it expects to clear within 2-3 weeks. Geopolitical risk is monitored industry-wide.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 investment plan and what is the Norton spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Overseas investment is about INR 2,400 crores in FY26 (mainly Norton) and is expected to be about 70% of that in FY27. Total FY27 capex is about INR 3,500 crores, of which about INR 2,000 crores is product development.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV capacity and international EV plan?
qa_highlights.answer: EV output is about 40,000 units per month, moving toward 50,000. Asian markets are taking a growing share of EV volumes, with iQube and Orbiter launched there.

qa_highlights.question: Will Norton products be made in India, and what is the Hyundai EV 3W partnership?
qa_highlights.answer: One high-end Norton model will be built at Solihull and the others in India, using the Hosur plant. The Hyundai JDA is for co-developing an EV 3W, with Hyundai leading design; management gave no revenue or timeline details.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation of 3-5% of revenue with only about 35% offset so far; margin sustainability beyond Q1 FY27 is uncertain.
Supply-chain disruption from gas prices, Tier 2 labour shortages and raw material timing; management expects normalisation in 2-3 weeks.
International container lead times up about 15%, with West Asia conflict and logistics delays affecting distributor planning.
Economy segment demand pressure from inflation and fuel prices; El Nino risk to rainfall and rural demand in Q3-Q4.
Norton and other overseas investments (about INR 2,400 crores in FY26) must yield revenue; Norton launches expected in Q2 FY27.

Answers on margins and the Hyundai partnership were deliberately high-level, with detail deferred to launch.

Immediately, we are looking at increasing the capacity by another 1.5 million, to go to somewhere around 8.3 million because the demand is good

532343|2026-06.headline: TVS Motor Q1 FY27 revenue rose 38% to INR 13,896 crore and operating EBITDA rose 41% to INR 1,779 crore, with margin at 12.8%.
532343|2026-06.overview: Total volume grew 28% YoY to 1.63 million units, with revenue of INR 13,896 crore (+38%) and PAT of INR 1,174 crore (+51%). Operating EBITDA margin expanded 30 bps to 12.8%, helped by price increases and cost actions despite a sharp commodity spike linked to the West Asia conflict. International sales hit a record 4.68 lakh units (+33%), and EV sales grew 86%. Management guided Q2 as better than Q1 and expects FY27 industry growth in double digits, with capacity expansion to 8.3 million 2W units by Q4.

financial_highlights.change: +51% YoY (INR 1,050 crore); includes ~INR 150 crore fair value gain vs ~INR 28 crore last year

segments.name: 2-wheeler domestic ICE
segments.commentary: Sales grew 21% YoY versus industry growth of 13%. Overall 2W ICE grew 23% against industry growth of 21%.

segments.name: 2-wheeler EV
segments.commentary: Volume rose to 130,000 units from 70,000 in the prior-year quarter, up 86%. June EV penetration was above 10.6%, and management said EV penetration in 3W crossed 40%.

segments.name: 2-wheeler international
segments.commentary: International market ICE sales grew 31%. Africa, Asia and LATAM contributed, with HLX crossing 5 million cumulative units.

segments.name: 3-wheeler
segments.commentary: Total sales rose 48% to 67,000 units from 45,000 units.

segments.name: TVS Credit
segments.commentary: Disbursed to over 14 lakh new customers, taking the customer base to about 2.6 crore. Book size grew 19% and PBT rose 16% to INR 283 crore.

segments.name: Norton
segments.commentary: Manx and Atlas production has started, with Atlas rolling out from Hosur in June. Cumulative investment is about INR 2,000 crore to INR 2,500 crore over the last 4-5 years.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 expected to be better than Q1; 2W ICE growth could be slightly better than Q1 and EV growth similar or slightly better.
Management expects FY27 industry growth of at least double digits in ICE, with EV growth well above penetration levels of about 10.6%.
International growth expected at the same rate or slightly better in Q2.
Price increases of about 1.5% were taken in Q1 and about 0.5% are planned in Q2, subject to market conditions.
Q3 is the key watch item due to El Nino, the base effect and GST benefits starting late September.
Festive season launches are planned for October and November.
capex_capacity: 2W capacity is planned to rise from about 6.8 million to 8.3 million units by Q4 FY27, in stages over Q2 and Q3.
3W capacity is planned to rise from about 0.25 million to about 0.42 million units, with a good share in EV.
Total capex, including new products and capacity expansion, is about INR 3,500 crore.
Capacity additions take about 3 to 4 months to commission.
Partnership with IOC for last-mile LPG cylinder distribution and cargo EV mobility.
demand_pricing: Commodity costs rose about 3.5% in Q1 and about 0.5% more in Q2, a total of about 4%; about 30% was passed through as per the last call.
Dealer inventory is kept at 25-30 days, with up to about 30 days during the festive season.
Management says it keeps less than 30 days of stock with dealers and cites JD Power rankings of No. 1 and No. 2 in the scooter category.
Scooter category share is about 40% including ICE and EV.
Production was disrupted in April by supply issues but recovered in May and June.
PLI incentive is about 0.6-0.7% of turnover, and about INR 600 crore of PLI is receivable.
Exports are about 26% of turnover; management aims to grow this materially.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV capacity and how is EV demand developing?
qa_highlights.answer: Two-wheeler capacity is about 40,000 units moving to 50,000+. 3W capacity is moving from about 20,000 to 30,000 units, with EV a good share. EV demand is spreading from urban to semi-urban areas, and some buyers are moving from motorcycles to scooters.

qa_highlights.question: Why is TVS gaining share against a competitor discounting in scooters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a broad scooter range, frequent feature upgrades, durability and JD Power rankings. It said dealer stock is kept below 30 days and that retail financing supports growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the commodity headwind and how much has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Most of the impact was in Q1, with some further pressure from aluminium and oil-linked plastics. Price increases were about 1.5% in Q1 and about 0.5% in Q2, with the rest offset by mix, scale and cost reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Is EV profitability improving?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EV contribution is improving quarter after quarter, but it expects the EV margin to reach the company's target over time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the overall capacity and investment plan?
qa_highlights.answer: 2W capacity is moving from about 6.8 million to 8.3 million units by Q4, with 3W capacity rising to about 0.42 million. Total investment is about INR 3,500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Norton strategy, investment and volume ambition?
qa_highlights.answer: Four Norton models (Manx, Manx R, Atlas and Atlas GT) are launching across the UK, Europe, India and later the US. The model uses independent dealers and multi-brand premium outlets, with cumulative investment of about INR 2,000-2,500 crore. Management gave no breakeven volume.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses decline and will that continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said April production loss and supply issues drove some cost control. It said brand spend as a percentage of sales will not change much, and launch costs will add to expenses when new products are introduced.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 600-700 crore PLI receivable collectible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR 600 crore is PLI receivable and is fully collectible, with the government having always supported the scheme.

risks_watch: Commodity volatility from the West Asia conflict (aluminium, steel, oil-linked plastics) and a possible further 0.5% cost pressure in Q2.
Supply chain availability, which was disrupted in April.
Q3 demand risks from El Nino, the high base from last year's GST effect and monsoon progression.
Draft Delhi EV policy may ban ICE 2-wheeler sales from around 2028.
Receivables of about INR 600-700 crore, mainly PLI, that need to be collected.
Norton ramp-up and breakeven volumes, which were not disclosed.
Q1 PBT includes about INR 150 crore of fair value gains that are non-operating.
Deep Vakil asked about gearing and a preference share redemption on 1 September; management did not answer this.

key_quotes: The company's operating EBITDA margin improved by 30 basis points at 12.8% during the first quarter and this is against 12.5% last year first quarter.
So, as a year, we should estimate an industry growth of double digit.
Yes, INR 600 crores is about PLI, that's a receivable.

rows.why: Q2 2W ICE growth guided slightly better than Q1's 21%, EV growth similar or slightly better than Q1's 86%, international growth same or slightly better, and FY27 industry growth at least double digit.
