rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided Q2 as better than Q1 and FY27 industry growth at double digit, with Q1 volume up 28% and 2W ICE up 23% versus industry 21%, though Q3 faces El Nino, high base and GST timing risks.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q3 is flagged as the key watch item due to El Nino, the high base from last year's GST effect and monsoon progression, and commodity costs could add about 0.5% more pressure in Q2.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Festive season launches are planned for October and November, and four Norton models (Manx, Manx R, Atlas, Atlas GT) are rolling out across UK, Europe, India and later the US, with Manx and Atlas already in production.

rows.label: PLI receivable of ~INR 600 crore collection
rows.why: About INR 600 crore of PLI (about 0.6-0.7% of turnover) is receivable, which management says is fully collectible, though the company did not give a timeline and analysts pressed on it.

rows.label: International growth and exports push
rows.why: International sales hit a record 4.68 lakh units (+33%), with international growth guided at the same or slightly better rate in Q2, and exports (INR 3,634 crore, about 26% of turnover) to grow materially.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, share gains (scooter share about 40%, JD Power No.1/No.2), exports and Q2, and cautious on commodity costs and Q3 timing; analysts pushed on Norton breakeven, PLI receivables and gearing, which management was evasive on.

532343|2026-09.headline: TVS Motor Q2 FY27 revenue rose 44% to INR17,103 crores and PAT 52% to INR1,377 crores, alongside approval of a consumer finance demerger.
532343|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 delivered record volume (1.9 million units, up 27%), revenue, EBITDA and profit, with EBITDA margin up 30 bps to 13.0%. Management said domestic 2W ICE and EV and 3W all grew faster than industry, and international sales hit a record 5.39 lakh units (up 35%). The Board approved a demerger of the consumer finance and related undertaking (including the TVS Credit Services stake) into a separate listed holding company, with shareholders receiving mirror shareholding; completion is expected around July 2027 appointed date after 8 to 10 months of approvals. Management guided to single-digit industry growth in H2 with base effects, and cost pressure expected to ease in Q3 and Q4.

segments.name: Domestic 2W
segments.commentary: Total 2W ICE sales grew 20% YoY vs industry 14%; domestic ICE up 16% vs industry 10%. Domestic 2W EV up 129% vs industry 84%. EV penetration of 2W was 11.6% in September (scooters about 22%).

segments.name: Domestic 3W
segments.commentary: ICE plus EV 3W volume about 26,300 units, up 65% from 16,000 vs industry 23%. EV penetration of 3W about 44% in Q2 and about 48% in September.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Record 5.39 lakh units in H1, up 35% YoY; Q2 international 2W ICE up 33% vs industry 27%. International EV sales about 6,930 units in Q2 vs 1,726 last year. Africa was the key driver.

segments.name: TVS Credit (consumer finance)
segments.commentary: Book size INR33,818 crores, up 22% from INR27,807 crores; PBT INR330 crores, up 19% from INR277 crores. Network over 65,000 touch points; 14 lakh new customers in the quarter; customer base about 2.7 crores.

segments.name: Norton (e-bike)
segments.commentary: Manx R and Atlas launches under way in Europe (dealers in UK, Italy, France; Germany and Spain coming); India launch expected in coming months; US preparations underway. Current-quarter e-bike loss is lower than the prior quarter, though brand and launch costs rose.

guidance_outlook: Industry ICE growth in 2W and 3W expected to be single digit in H2 FY27 given the high base from Nov-Dec last year; management said it would wait a couple of weeks for a clearer Q3 view.
TVS expects to outgrow the industry in domestic and international markets in Q3 and Q4.
Material cost increases expected to be unlikely in Q3 and Q4 beyond small increases; Q4 may stabilise or soften.
Capacity: 2W capacity to exceed 8 million units and 3W to reach about 0.4 million soon; EV capacity at 60,000-65,000 units per month now, with plans for about 80,000.
Demerger appointed date is July 2027; approvals (regulatory, shareholder, NCLT) expected to take 8 to 10 months. Management to give FY28-FY29 investment guidance next quarter.
capex_capacity: EV capacity at about 60,000-65,000 units per month (domestic plus exports), with next-level expansion to about 80,000 planned and under way; Orbiter capacity to be enhanced in Q4.
2W capacity to cross 8 million units; 3W capacity to reach about 0.4 million soon.
Capacity expansion lead time for new models is about 3 months, per management.
Management said capacity planning for next year is starting now, given market pull and longer-range planning needs.

Additional INR1,200 crores equity infusion into TVS Credit Services is planned before the demerger, depending on capital requirements; INR711 crores was a secondary purchase of TVS Credit shares during the quarter.
demand_pricing: Dealer inventory held at 21-30 days (management said under 30 days, with many dealers under 21 days); cash-and-carry model.
Price actions: Q1 to Q2 material costs rose about 1.9% and selling prices rose 1.6%; small price increases taken early in Q3, with another review after Diwali.
EV industry grew about 75% in H1 per management; scooters share of category about 41% including EV, with ICE scooters at about 32-33%.
Ronin volume expected to go beyond 15,000 units, per management.
PLI benefit about 1.3-1.4% of turnover; management said the company has crossed the 10,000 cumulative mark and is on track for the higher incentive slab.

qa_highlights.question: How is TVS building EV capacity given supply constraints, and what is the Ronin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: EV industry grew about 75% in H1; capacity now 60,000-65,000 units/month, with 80,000 planned. Ronin is expected to go beyond 15,000 units per month, with new variants and a large capacity investment under way.

qa_highlights.question: What is the structure of the consumer finance demerger and what holdings will TVS Motor keep?
qa_highlights.answer: Demerged undertaking includes the TVS Credit Services investment and some non-core investments, moved to a new company with mirror shareholding. TVS Motor keeps no stake; the TVS Credit business is not being merged into the new entity.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for the demerger listing?
qa_highlights.answer: Post shareholder approval and NCLT process, around 8 to 10 months. The appointed date is July 2027, after the NBFC consolidation mandated by RBI (approvals expected by March or April 2027).

qa_highlights.question: What is the valuation and net worth of TVS Credit?
qa_highlights.answer: No valuation is set in a demerger. Net worth is about INR6,500 crores before the proposed INR1,200 crore equity infusion. Management declined to give ROE and ROA figures.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for industry growth in H2 and pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Single-digit growth expected in Q3 given a high base. Material costs expected to rise less in Q3 and Q4; Q1 to Q2 prices rose 1.6% vs 1.9% material cost increase.

qa_highlights.question: Are EV e-bike losses coming down outside Norton?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-Norton e-mobility losses have been curtailed and will be cut further. The Norton loss is lower than in the prior quarter, but brand and launch costs rose.

risks_watch: Base effect in Nov-Dec: management flagged a high prior-year base, making H2 growth more cautious (single digit expected).
Commodity cost inflation: Q1 to Q2 material costs rose about 1.9%; price actions need to keep pace, and employee and marketing costs rose sharply.
Norton and the e-bike business continue to lose money; cumulative losses about INR1,300 crores over 4-5 years per an analyst; India launch and US plans still pending.
Demerger execution: 8 to 10 months to approvals, NBFC consolidation under RBI direction, and the July 2027 appointed date. Business split and valuation are not yet disclosed.
Next quarter: Q3 volume and EBITDA trends after Diwali, EV capacity ramp to 80,000, and FY28-29 investment guidance.

I'm pretty confident that our products will do very well even the next year, financial year.
I'm of the view that I think we have to look at together scooters.

532348|2026-03.headline: Subex Q4 FY26 revenue rose 3% QoQ to INR 72.96 crores, with EBITDA margin at 14.5% and FY26 order intake up 24%.
532348|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 72.96 crores versus INR 70.79 crores in Q3, with EBITDA of INR 10.58 crores (14.5% margin) and normalized PAT of INR 11.51 crores. Management said FY26 full-year total income grew 6% YoY, partly supported by interest income, and that FY25 is not like-for-like because non-core businesses were exited. Order intake grew 24% in FY26 and management highlighted AI deal wins, though it acknowledged top-line growth lagged its ambitions. Middle East exposure, the geopolitical backdrop and slow new-purchase decisions were flagged as the main near-term risks, with revenue conversion expected to improve as implementations finish.

segments.name: Products
segments.commentary: Four core products: Revenue Assurance, Fraud Management, Partner Settlement (wholesale billing) and Enterprise Asset Management. FraudZap is the newer AI fraud product, with one paid customer that onboarded three Telcos through an intermediary.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Management said about 31% of revenue comes from the Gulf region, and that APAC and Europe are steady. Africa is seeing momentum and the Americas will get heavy investment in FY27.

guidance_outlook: No formal numerical FY27 guidance was given; management described the team as 'very bullish' and said it expects to beat FY26 results.
Management expects revenue conversion to improve quarter by quarter as implementations of FY26 wins finish, with an uptick expected around the middle of FY27 if there are no delays.
INR 100 crores per quarter revenue was described internally as a target ('war cry'), with no timeline committed.
Management plans to pursue tuck-in acquisitions in FY27, which the board is actively discussing.
Management said the goodwill impairment test is complete and auditors found no impairment needed on carrying value of about INR 190 crores.
capex_capacity: Team of LLMs product has completed POCs and is in talks with two or three customers to go commercial this quarter, but GPU hardware constraints are slowing deployment.
Management is working on running agents on CPU or a laptop-sized 'agent in a box' to get around the GPU constraint; it said it is also looking at neuromorphic hardware.
GenAI-based software development is being embedded across the MCLC to lift developer productivity and reduce engineering cost.
key_quotes: I'll be direct anytime that you ask that question of me.
So, I believe that the reset is done. The foundation is built and FY27 is where we will convert it.
I truly believe that the stock is materially undervalued related to our fundamentals and our trajectory.

qa_highlights.answer: Legacy MS and AMC products carry the margins described earlier. Management declined to give product-level margins because they are competition-sensitive.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Gulf region hit the business and what share of revenue is it?
qa_highlights.answer: A management response put the Gulf share at about 31% of revenue. APAC and Europe are steady. Management said the main risk is delay in new purchases, not renewals.

qa_highlights.question: Is the goodwill write-off a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: The annual impairment test is complete. Auditors found the carrying value is fine and no write-off is needed.

qa_highlights.answer: Management is discussing tuck-in acquisitions with the board. It is not divesting OnGrid because the investee is doing well and the company has enough cash for its own bets.

532348|2026-06.headline: Subex Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19.7% YoY to INR 79.45 crore, with EBITDA margin at 21.2% and management signalling margins will be held in a range.
532348|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 8.9% QoQ and 19.7% YoY to INR 79.45 crore, with EBITDA of INR 16.87 crore (21.2% margin) versus INR 10.58 crore in Q4. Normalized PAT was INR 16.09 crore versus INR 11.51 crore previously, and reported PAT was INR 14.22 crore. Management framed FY27 as a growth year, while saying it will hold margins in a range and reinvest excess cash in R&D and AI. Cash stood at INR 184.8 crore, and management declined to give a funnel number, order-book value or a revenue target, citing competitive sensitivity.

segments.commentary: Management called it an under-invested business that has been rebuilt; it renewed a Tier 1 Asia-Pacific PEM engagement this quarter and sees stronger deal flow. No quantified revenue was given.

segments.name: RAFM (Revenue Assurance and Fraud Management)
segments.commentary: Secured new business assurance and fraud management deal with a leading European operator; a FraudZap customer deal was said to be slipping into this quarter. Management said FraudZap's investment is already recovered, though no margin figure was given.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance. Management said it will not give forward guidance on the call; expects 'double-digit' or 'high single digit' growth, to be decided.
Margins to be held 'in the ballpark' of the FY26 close and the mid-to-high teens was not confirmed; management will hold margins in a range and reinvest excess cash in R&D/AI.
R&D intensity to rise; target horizon split of 60/30/10 (H1/H2/H3) over the next two years.
Management aims to reach INR 100 crore quarterly top line in 'a few quarters' with backlog-driven visibility; no date committed.
Board is considering capital restructuring (reducing equity against losses) via a consultant, with board, shareholder and NCLT approvals needed; long process.
ESOP: 5% approved; up to 2% to be acquired from market in FY27, with execution expected around Q3 after postal ballot.
capex_capacity: R&D headcount about 700 in total, with about 200 in core R&D teams.
Middle East delivery offshored to Bangalore; on-site resources in Dubai, Kuwait and Qatar pulled back.
Implementation cycle from contract to subscription revenue is 4-5 quarters; internal goal to cut by one quarter, with recent project closed about 45 days early.

Q2 FY27 fair value markup planned for the stake in an unlisted company received on sale of ID Central.
demand_pricing: Qualified pipeline stated at 3-4x the annual order-intake target; management said 70% of revenue is recurring and 30% is won in-year.
Middle East: slowdown in orders and deal timing, not cancellations; a Tier 1 Middle East renewal was secured.
US described as better; Europe described as okay; APAC and Africa described as slower; contracts slipping by a month or two.
Deals above USD 0.8-1 million go through RFP; management would not disclose margin thresholds for contract acceptance.
Management said FY26 announced deals were about INR 18-20 million (unclear units; transcript says 'in the range of five' then '18-20 million').

qa_highlights.answer: CEO said it was discussed at the board meeting held the day before; a consultant will be appointed, and it is a long process requiring board, shareholder and NCLT approval.

qa_highlights.question: Size of executable pipeline and total order wins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave qualified pipeline at 3-4x target but declined to give absolute numbers, citing competitive sensitivity.

qa_highlights.question: Where will EBITDA margins stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins expected 'in the ballpark' of current levels; management will not cap margins but will reinvest excess cash in R&D and AI.

qa_highlights.question: Middle East exposure and sectoral contract recoveries?
qa_highlights.answer: Sectoral contract litigation continues: one of three entities settled, two others being chased for closure this quarter; the remaining one is in Middle East courts with no firm timeline. Middle East subsidiary is self-sufficient, with no further capital infusion expected.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the revenue increase was FX?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO estimated about INR 3 crore of currency gain in the quarter; QoQ FX gain was small.

qa_highlights.question: Acquisition and ESOP timing?
qa_highlights.answer: ESOP: postal ballot planned within about two weeks; purchases expected around Q3 for up to 2% in FY27. Inorganic options under review, but no active talks.

532348|2026-09.headline: Subex Q2 FY27 revenue rose 7.7% QoQ to INR 85.59 crore (+24% YoY), with normalized EBITDA of INR 17.77 crore and a fifth straight QoQ growth quarter.
532348|2026-09.overview: Revenue grew 7.7% QoQ to INR 85.59 crore from INR 79.45 crore, marking five consecutive quarters of QoQ growth per management. Normalized EBITDA rose to INR 17.77 crore from INR 16.87 crore despite the annual wage increase, while normalized PAT fell to INR 14.3 crore from INR 16.9 crore; reported PAT was INR 14.29 crore versus INR 14.22 crore. Cash and equivalents rose to INR 198 crore from INR 184 crore. Management spent most of the call on a strategic repositioning toward AI-led "integrity of decisions" and economic integrity, while declining to give quantitative guidance.

532349|2026-06.headline: TCI Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue grew ~9% (24th straight quarter of growth) while standalone profit turned slightly negative on lower JV dividends and bunker costs.
532349|2026-06.overview: Management reported 9% consolidated top-line growth and 7% standalone growth for Q1 FY27, with the freight business up 10-11%. Standalone EBITDA margin was about 1.6% and PAT slightly negative, largely because JV dividend income was lower; consolidated EBITDA was about 5%. Management guided supply chain to 12-15% growth and freight to 10-12%, with capex of Rs 550-600 crore for FY27 (Rs 167 crore spent in Q1).

segments.name: Freight
segments.commentary: Top line up ~10-11% with slight margin improvement; 10 of planned 30 new branches opened in Q1. FY27 guidance 10-12% growth with higher profitability.

segments.commentary: Grew ~88% per management; revenue moderated vs last quarter per Q&A. Rail shift from road limited due to lean season and rail congestion.

segments.name: Cold Chain JV
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~48% from contracts won in Q3-Q4 FY26; still small in quantum.

segments.name: Trans System JV (Toyota-linked, Mitsui partner)

Sugar: management sees 'excellent' sugar pricing ahead, with pricing expected to hold at current levels; domestic sugar consumption estimated at 28.3 MT by Triveni versus government estimate of 28.1 MT.

Ethanol: management estimates next-year (ESY 2026-27) ethanol procurement of about 1,300 crore litres and expects a roughly 3:1 grain-to-sugary feedstock ratio; expects Triveni to match that mix via multi-feed distilleries.
Water: management expects to achieve the year's operating plan, though execution is lumpy; recent tenders are under pursuit.
Management said there is sufficient country-liquor capacity for at least the next three quarters.
capex_capacity: Sugar crush for 2025-26 was 8.25 million MT, down about 9% YoY on poorer yields and higher diversion; gross recovery improved 26 bps to 11.1%.

Some CapEx has gone into sugar plant cost efficiency (steam economics, bagasse savings) for the upcoming season.
Management will maximise crystallisation capacity for sugar next year rather than divert juice to ethanol in UP.
Capital allocation review is under active examination by the board; management said water needs better ROCE before more capital, and country liquor needs little capital but is capped by UP geography.
demand_pricing: Sugar prices: refined sugar about ₹4,600/quintal and sulphitation sugar about ₹4,525/quintal as of the call date, versus the previous-quarter average.

Industry closing stock for 2025-26 estimated at about 4 MT, the lowest since Sept 2017 (3.88 MT).
Sugar cane price (SAP) hike last season was ₹30/quintal, the highest ever; management is uncertain about SAP for the next season given UP elections in early 2027.

Maize prices rose in the single-digit percentage range over four to five months; DDGS realisation offsets the maize rise. MP maize procurement expected from November; current maize is covered until Oct–Nov.
Country liquor is a competitive market; Triveni claims top-five position in UP. Branded spirits (about 5-6% of volume) are growing but unprofitable.

qa_highlights.question: Expected sugarcane yields going forward after the lower 2025-26 crush?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 2025-26 output fell about 9% on poorer yields and higher diversion, partly offset by higher recoveries. For 2026-27 it reported pest and disease incidence well below monitoring lines and adequate rainfall at five of eight factories, while stressing the next six weeks of grand growth are critical.

qa_highlights.question: What are the bottlenecks in the water business execution (Prayagraj etc.) and how will they be resolved?
qa_highlights.answer: Suresh Taneja called the slippage part of the business's lumpy execution and said the company should still achieve the full-year operating plan.

qa_highlights.question: How will Maharashtra and Karnataka cane output and national sugar balance look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a flattish performance in Maharashtra and Karnataka, with limited upside. It estimates FY27 domestic consumption at 28.3 MT against the government's 28.1 MT, and says sugar supply is sufficient.

qa_highlights.question: Will mills divert more cane juice or B-heavy to ethanol and cut sugar output, and what diversion is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Triveni will maximise crystallisation capacity in UP next year. Diversion is expected to be between zero and 3 MT, with B-heavy likely to be diverted and juice diversion uncertain until October 2026 cane estimates.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ethanol offtake fall, and will capacity utilisation stay below 70%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ethanol procurement was above 1,100 crore litres this year and expects about 1,300 crore litres next year. It expects standalone distilleries running at 20-50% utilisation to face viability pressure once interest moratoriums end, so utilisation will vary by group and multi-feed capacity matters.

qa_highlights.question: Maize price outlook and cost cover?
qa_highlights.answer: Maize prices rose in the single-digit percentage range over four to five months, offset by higher DDGS realisation. Procurement covers until October-November, and MP maize is expected from November.

qa_highlights.question: Sir Shadi Lal standalone numbers and recovery outlook; debt and capital allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Sir Shadi Lal is amalgamated, so separate EBITDA and PAT are not disclosed. FY26 crush was 82 lakh quintals at 10.4% recovery, with a rebound expected in 2026-27. Working capital borrowings are expected lower; the board is examining capital allocation, with water needing better ROCE and country liquor capped by UP geography.

risks_watch: Monsoon and grand growth period over the next six weeks for Triveni's eight sugar units, particularly Rani Nangal and Sabitgarh with lower rainfall, and El Nino risk to cane yields and recoveries.

UP cane price (SAP) decision ahead of the early-2027 UP elections, given the record ₹30/quintal hike last season and existing arrears.
Government stock limits (4,000 quintals, 30 days) for 1 Aug–30 Nov 2026 and any further intervention if prices rise.
Water execution lumpiness: revenue fell 21% and the order book of ₹1,472 crore must convert; watch the L1 wins from over ₹300 crore of bids.

Branded spirits remain unprofitable; country liquor is hit by UP excise quota revisions and penalty changes. TPTL listing expected in four to six weeks, subject to approvals, with figures not yet disclosed.

532356|2026-09.headline: Triveni H1 FY27 PBT swung to ₹131 crore from a ₹25 crore loss, driven by sugar realisations up 9% to ₹4,428/MT.
532356|2026-09.overview: Consolidated H1 FY27 revenue rose 5% YoY to ₹3,311 crore and operating margin expanded 383 bps to 6.9%, with PBT of ₹131 crore versus a loss of ₹25 crore. Q2 revenue rose 8% to ₹1,731 crore. Sugar drove the turnaround on higher realisations, lower inventory and lower finance cost, while net debt fell to ₹157 crore from ₹702 crore a year ago. Management flagged a mixed H2: tight domestic sugar stocks support prices, but the ESY 26-27 ethanol tender resets alcohol economics and the Water business needs faster execution.

segments.name: Sugar

segments.name: Alcohol (Distillery)
segments.commentary: H1 revenue up 3%, PBIT up 44%; Q2 net revenue up 19% on 16% higher volume. H1 production 1,085 lakh litres, down 13% YoY, due to fewer operating days, storage constraints and a shift away from B-heavy molasses. Grain-based ethanol is the largest component.

segments.name: Water

guidance_outlook: Sugar: management expects prevailing prices (about ₹5,800/quintal institutional, ₹5,400/quintal trade) to hold for the next couple of quarters, subject to no new government price or sale regulation; flagged a slight downward bias in the short term.

Alcohol: Q3 FY27 seen as relatively unabated versus internal estimates; Q4 FY27 profitability is hard to call until the ESY 26-27 tender is finalised. Maize at ₹26-27/kg may fully erode maize-ethanol profitability for standalone plants.
Water: expects execution to pick up in Q3 and Q4 FY27 and return to budgeted levels.
Capex: no meaningful capex planned for the year beyond minor steam and efficiency measures; board to wait at least one quarter of cash generation before evaluating other capital allocation options.

Management's own estimate of domestic 2026-27 net sugar production is about 27.5 million MT with downside risk, against opening stocks of about 3.5 million MT and consumption of about 28.5 million MT.
capex_capacity: Chandanpur plant started crushing on the call day (3 Nov 2026); Sabitgarh expected to start the next day, Khatauli on 6 Nov, and remaining plants shortly after Deepawali. Group has eight UP factories.
Early-season recoveries are running about 50-70 bps lower YoY on sampling data for UP as a whole; management says two of its eight factories are sharply affected while six are broadly fine.
Share of 238 cane variety is under 30% group-wide, with East UP near zero and Central UP single digit; management plans a sharp cut in the next planting.
Chandanpur and other factories' sugar recoveries will be confirmed by lab data after crushing begins; mid-December to mid-January is the window for a clear crop-impact assessment.
demand_pricing: Raw sugar import parity into Delhi, without margin, is about ₹54.5/kg; white sugar parity is about ₹59.15/kg (Dec contract) and ₹60.7/kg (Mar contract).
India has an import allowance of 1 million MT; about 300,000 MT has been imported so far. Management expects a further allowance of at least 2 million MT, mainly raw sugar.

October domestic prices averaged about ₹49/kg before rising sharply in November. Haryana SAP raised by ₹15 to ₹430/quintal for 26-27 and ₹20 to ₹450 for 27-28; UP cane price announcement expected in about three to four weeks.

ESY 26-27 OMC tender: 1,100 crore litres offered, with no offers for juice, syrup or B-heavy molasses ethanol. FCI rice capped at 30% (vs about 40% last year). Maize ethanol price cut by ₹3/litre in the tender.
Management's first-tranche split: ₹150 crore C-heavy, ₹324 crore FCI rice, up to ₹160 crore DFG, and about ₹466 crore maize (implied). Triveni's ethanol capacity is about 25 crore litres.

Global: raw sugar moved from $0.1331/lb (April low) to a $0.213 high and is about $0.195/lb; white sugar from $376/t to $561/t, now about $520/t. Brazil crop rebound and crude above $100/bbl are the key swing factors.

qa_highlights.question: How much damage has late UP rainfall done to the crop, and how does it compare with Maharashtra and Karnataka?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said damage is hard to quantify and could come as yield loss (lodging) or sucrose loss. Western UP cane is bound, so lodging risk is low. Sampling data shows about 50-70 bps lower recovery YoY for the state, with a clearer read by mid-December to mid-January.

qa_highlights.question: Will the tender-based ethanol economics hold once maize prices stay high?
qa_highlights.answer: Current maize at ₹26-27/kg would fully erode maize-ethanol profitability for standalone plants; integrated multi-feed players are better placed. Triveni procured maize at lower prices earlier, so Q3 is secure, and Q4 depends on the final tender.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for UP cane price and sugar import volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: UP cane price expected around end-November, with no number given. About 300,000 MT of the 1 million MT import allowance has been used, with at least 2 million MT more expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise despite the power transmission demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Suresh Taneja said last year's comparatives show power transmission costs under discontinued operations, so the like-for-like comparison shows no significant increase. Management attributed the rise to the new labour code revising wages for 4,000-plus employees.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company deploy capital given high profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: No meaningful capex is planned. Debt reduction is a priority, but the board wants at least one quarter of cash generation data before deciding on other options.

532365|2026-03.headline: Dynacons FY26 revenue rose about 12% to INR1,424 crore and EBITDA about 41% to INR146 crore, but Q4 EBITDA margin fell to about 9% on cost pressure.
532365|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue from operations of INR402 crore (about 22% YoY) and EBITDA of INR36 crore (about 26% YoY). Full-year EBITDA margin rose to 10.2% from 8.1%, and PAT grew about 17% to INR85 crore. Management attributed the Q4 sequential margin dip to AI-driven component cost escalation and supply tightness, which it expects to normalise. Order book was close to INR3,000 crore as of May 30, 2026, and the bidding pipeline was about INR5,100 crore as of May 2026. Analysts pressed on lease-driven depreciation and finance cost, working capital days and unit economics of the as-a-service deals; management declined to disclose IRR, payback, segment order book mix or go-live values.

532365|2026-06.headline: Dynacons Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR313 crore (from INR328 crore) on OEM-linked delivery delays, while EBITDA rose to INR40 crore and order book reached INR3,104 crore.
532365|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations declined year-on-year to INR313 crore from INR328 crore, which management attributed to extended OEM and supply-chain lead-times deferring execution and revenue recognition rather than weaker demand. EBITDA rose to INR40 crore, PAT was about INR20 crore and EPS was INR15.54, and management cited a better business mix and higher-value infrastructure and services. Order inflows were strong, including a INR750 crore RBI private cloud mandate, a INR267 crore NPCI data-centre project and a INR125 crore CBI AI-ready infrastructure mandate, taking the order book to about INR3,104 crore. Management declined to give numeric guidance, and analysts pressed on margins, lease costs, ROCE on the as-a-service asset base and competition from Netweb.

guidance_outlook: FY29 (Lakshya) EBITDA margin target raised to about 30% from 27%; FY29 revenue target kept at INR20,000 crore (about 4x FY26).
Management aims to perform at or above the Q2 operational margin of 27% from Q3 FY27 onwards.
Net working capital cycle to stay in the 45-50 day range; debtor and inventory improvement expected from next quarter.
Net finance cost expected to fall from Q3 FY27 after early loan prepayments.
Capex of about INR1,000 crore per year from FY27 to FY29, for a 50% expansion of preform, fiber and cable capacity and a greenfield preterm solutions facility.
R&D commitment of 2% of annual revenue for next-generation optical platforms.
risks_watch: Q2 reported EBITDA includes a one-off INR161 crore tariff refund gain; operational margin of 27.1% is the true base.
Supply-constrained raw materials (germanium, helium) and lower payable days; working capital cycle is at the upper end of the 45-50 day range.
Execution risk on the INR35,274 crore order book from hyperscaler capex timing, interest rates, and local land, power and water constraints.
Customer concentration in hyperscaler contracts; management did not disclose the attach-rate contribution or the DC fiber revenue split.
Hollow-core and multi-core fiber commercial scale-up is 1.5-2 years away, so near-term revenue from these is limited.
Interest cost rose 15% YoY in Q2 with receivables up; management expects lower net finance cost from Q3 FY27.
532374|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, order book and margin trajectory, with the margin upgrade tied to the order book and mix. Management was evasive on pricing, utilisation percentages, DC attach revenue and attach-rate targets, citing competitive reasons.
key_quotes: So what we've done for now is basically looked at the order book that we have and the improvements in our order book that we have showcased going to INR35,000 crores.
Our open order book stands at record INR35,274 crores, up 4.6x from INR7,687 crores at the start of this financial year.
we are upgrading our FY '29 EBITDA margin target to about 30%, up from 27% earlier, while maintaining our FY '29 revenue target at INR20,000 crores.
I'm pleased to report that our attach rate has reached an all-time high of 24% in H1 FY '27, up from 20% in H1 FY '26.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin target upgrade to 30% while the INR20,000 crore revenue target was kept, and is a revenue target upgrade possible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the upgrade reflects the INR35,000 crore order book, a mix shift toward higher-margin data center products and a higher attach rate. The INR20,000 crore revenue target is retained, to be re-evaluated against order book execution and capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Reported EBITDA includes a INR161 crore US tariff refund; is more refund expected, and why did interest cost rise 15% YoY with receivables up, plus the INR49 crore impairment?
qa_highlights.answer: Most refunds have been received; Phase 3 is in process and a small amount has been applied for. The INR49 crore impairment and INR22 crore extra depreciation relate to subsidiary Speedon Networks, squared off in full. Some loans were prepaid early with penalties settled, and net finance cost is expected to fall from Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the DC fiber revenue and DC attach revenue contribution, and is attach revenue part of the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split DC fiber or DC attach revenue, citing competitive reasons. It confirmed that attach-rate revenue (accessories business) forms part of the reported order book. A good portion of the order book is DC, given the two large deals announced.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 margins be better than the 27% Q2 level, given H1 margin of about 23-24%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims to perform at or above the Q2 operational margin of 27% from Q3 FY27, and that the Lakshya plan aligns with the 30% FY29 target. Margin gains are attributed to the DC-heavy mix, which is more profitable than traditional Telco business.

qa_highlights.question: What is average utilisation and when will full utilisation be reached? Also, where does the company stand on DC share versus peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not disclose utilisation figures; it said utilisation is improving quarter on quarter after better raw material procurement and diversification. On DC share, management reiterated a target of about 50%, with 50-60% by design, and said it is cutting low-end commoditised fiber and cable sales.

qa_highlights.question: Risks to order book delivery timelines given US and global AI data center project delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is watching interest rates and hyperscaler cash positions, and flagged local execution challenges around land, power, water and local opposition. It said conversations have not changed, and hyperscalers are diversifying into the Nordics, India, Australia and Mongolia.

capex_capacity: Capex of about INR1,000 crore per year from FY27 to FY29, covering brownfield expansion of preform, fiber and cable capacity by 50% and a greenfield preterm solutions facility (CFO said total capex INR1,000 crore per year, 2027 to 2029).
Management said it is building a new greenfield site to increase termination capability, as part of the capex plan.
Utilisation is improving quarter on quarter after easing raw material constraints (germanium, helium); management did not give utilisation percentages.
Management wants to start executing capacity projects and bring them online in the next few quarters, and expects capacity coming up in the next 2 to 3 years to support further partnerships.
Hollow-core and multi-core fiber scale-up expected in roughly 1.5 to 2 years; HCF is in first commercial pilot phase.
demand_pricing: Order intake in H1 FY27 was about INR32,000 crore, roughly 4x the orders won in all of FY26; largest Q2 win is a new 5-year agreement with a potential value of $1.2 billion from a global hyperscaler for AI-ready optical solutions, following a $1.11 billion award last quarter.

Open order book INR35,274 crore, up 4.6x from INR7,687 crore at start of FY27; about INR3,021 crore scheduled for Q3 FY27, rest in Q4 FY27 and beyond. Order book spread across customer segments, product categories and geographies.
Spot business now a negligible share of revenue; revenue increasingly drawn from scheduled multiyear backlog with hyperscalers and telecom operators.
Data Center share was 33% of H1 FY27 revenue; management targets about 50% in the current fiscal and a 50-60% DC share by design. A good portion of the order book is DC-linked.
Global ex-China OFC market share rose to 9% in H1 FY27 from 7% in H1 FY26. Attach rate reached 24% in H1 FY27 vs 20% in H1 FY26, on a much larger OFC revenue base; target is 25% and beyond for FY27.
Market context cited from CRU: global optical cable demand expected to reach 851 million fiber km by 2031 (7.5% CAGR); CRU upgraded 2026 data center demand growth to 89% YoY from 63%.
Pricing: management declined to comment on prices, preform or fiber price trends, citing competitive reasons; focus is on high-end Neuralis cables and connectivity products (CONCAT, MMC).
Management did not disclose attach-rate contribution or DC fiber revenue split, citing competitive reasons.

532375|2026-03.headline: Tips Music Q4 FY26 revenue rose 32% YoY to INR103.9 crore and PAT 93% to INR59 crore; management targets 20% top-line and 20% bottom-line growth in FY27.
532375|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR103.9 crore (+32% YoY), operating EBITDA INR76.9 crore (+106% YoY) and PAT INR59 crore (+93% YoY), with management saying there were no one-offs. For FY26, revenue was INR375.5 crore (+21%) and PAT INR216.6 crore (+30%), and the company distributed INR166 crore in dividends. Digital was about 70% of FY26 revenue and non-digital about 30%, with brand publishing and public performance cited as growth contributors. Content cost fell to about 15.8% of revenue as a film's music release slipped from Q4 to June 2026. Management guided to 20% top-line and 20% bottom-line growth for FY27 and declined to raise that target further.

segments.name: Digital (incl. YouTube, subscriptions)
segments.commentary: About 70% of FY26 revenue; management said a couple of platform closures were a headwind at the start of the year. YouTube long-form views grew as expected while YouTube Shorts views declined, which management called non-material to revenue.

segments.name: Non-digital (publishing, public performance, brand)
segments.commentary: About 30% of FY26 revenue; brand publishing and public performance were cited as the main contributors, and the Q4 non-digital share rose versus earlier quarters.

guidance_outlook: FY27 target of 20% top-line and 20% bottom-line growth; management declined to raise it to 30%, saying it will review after one or two quarters.
Content spend guided at roughly 20% to 25% of top-line for FY27 (analyst figure confirmed by management).
Management said content cost could reach INR80 crore to INR90 crore in FY27, versus about INR60 crore in FY26 and INR70 crore to INR71 crore in FY25.
Two films, Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai and Main Vaapas Aaunga, are slated for theatrical release on 22 May and 12 June 2026; their music costs will be expensed in Q1 FY27 on release.
YouTube Shorts deal renewal is due around June 2026; negotiations were expected to start at end-April or early May 2026. Management said the view decline does not affect the renewal.
capex_capacity: Content slate for FY27 is in investor presentation Slide 8; management cited a David Dhawan film and an Imtiaz Ali and A.R. Rahman project.
Acquired Kutchchi Music (Gujarati label) with about 4,000 songs in roughly Q2 FY26 (July-August 2025).
Public performance licences are now available online, which management expects to drive growth.
Management is cautious on acquisitions because of high valuations.
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 release of 66 new songs (47 film, 19 non-film), with a focus on quality over quantity.
YouTube subscribers at 153 million; a catalogue song on Instagram reached 3 billion views and another 1.5 billion.
Management attributed the growth to the repertoire, with several catalogue songs trending across Instagram, YouTube and Spotify.
Public performance industry is about INR500 crore; management expects it to reach at least INR3,000 crore in about three years (over 50% CAGR).
Management said bundling with telecom packs gives lower payouts and prefers pure-play music platforms.
The company said the Warner Chappell India publishing setup is positive; it already works with Sony Publishing.
Management said the industry is growing at about 8%, against the company's 20% to 25%; the call attributed the gap to repertoire strength and streaming growth.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 32% Q4 growth, and were there any one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited the 90s repertoire and said there were no one-offs or adjustments; all revenue was recurring.

qa_highlights.question: Why did YouTube Shorts views decline, and does it affect the June 2026 renewal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline is normal, with viral spikes causing peaks, and sees no material impact on renewal. Negotiations start at the end of April or early May 2026, and no replacement has been named for Hari Nair.

qa_highlights.question: Why did content cost fall to 15.8% of revenue versus 23% last year, against an 18% target?
qa_highlights.answer: A film, Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai, had its music moved from January to June 2026, delaying content cost. Costs will be expensed when released in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will employee costs stay at the Q4 level?
qa_highlights.answer: No; the Q4 increase reflects the annual increment provision, and cost should return to Q2 and Q3 run rates.

qa_highlights.question: What is paid subscription's share of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Paid subscription is 10% to 15% of digital revenue, up from about 10% to 12% last year, and it is growing at 30% to 40% CAGR.

qa_highlights.question: Are there any advances or provisions to Tips Films in the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO declined to give details, but said the terms are arm's length. He said the album cost is fully expensed on release and nothing is carried on the balance sheet.

qa_highlights.question: Why are the FY27 growth targets only 20%, and will the company raise them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not want to over-promise and will revisit after one or two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue jump, and is the non-digital base in Q4 sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is seasonally low and Q3 and Q4 are stronger; publishing, public performance and brand revenue are expected to continue.

risks_watch: YouTube Shorts renewal in June 2026 after the departure of Hari Nair, with no replacement yet named.
Content cost is set to rise to INR80 crore to INR90 crore in FY27, which could pressure margins if the Q1 film releases underperform.
Digital share fell in Q4 and the mix relies on non-digital growth; management did not give the non-digital breakdown.
Related-party dealings with Tips Films; the CFO declined to give details of advances or liabilities.
Management says the music market is overvalued and will cool, which could limit acquisitions.
Management declined to disclose YouTube or Warner revenue split.

532375|2026-06.headline: Tips Music Q1 FY27 revenue rose 21% YoY to INR106.51 crores, but PAT fell 4% to INR43.89 crores as full content cost was expensed upfront.
532375|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 21% YoY to INR106.51 crores while content costs rose 90% YoY, since the entire cost of new releases was expensed in the quarter against revenue that only began mid-May. PAT was INR43.89 crores, down 4% YoY. Management maintained 20% revenue and PAT growth guidance for the year and said the full-year EBITDA margin should remain in the 65-70% range. A buyback board meeting was rescheduled to August 5, 2026, to evaluate open-market versus tender-offer options, with last year's PAT of INR217 crores to be returned via dividend and buyback.

segments.name: Digital
segments.commentary: Contributed around 75% of revenue in Q1 FY27; management would not split digital and non-digital growth separately.

segments.name: Non-digital
segments.commentary: Balance of about 25% of revenue; no separate figure or growth rate disclosed on the call.

guidance_outlook: Maintains 20% revenue and 20% PAT growth guidance for the year.
Full-year content budget of INR90-100 crores, versus the INR80-90 crores cited earlier; depends on movie release schedule.
EBITDA margin on an annual basis expected at 65-70%; quarterly aberrations possible due to content releases.

Content sourcing split roughly one-third outside production houses, one-third Tips Films, one-third internal non-film music.
demand_pricing: Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai crossed 186 million YouTube views; Chunnari Chunnari - Let's Go crossed 70 million; Main Vaapas Aaunga nearly 100 million.
Subscription is about 10-15% of revenue in India versus over 50% globally; paid subscribers growing 40-50% CAGR per management.
Spotify and YouTube raised prices around end of calendar 2025; management said Spotify's mid-May revision is not material to revenue.
YouTube Shorts renewal still under negotiation; update promised by end of Q2.
Amazon Music introduced a three-tier structure for non-Prime members.

qa_highlights.question: Will content costs stay at INR80-90 crores for the year given only about INR40 crores in Q1, and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year content budget is INR90-100 crores. EBITDA margin should be 65-70% on an annual basis; quarterly aberrations are possible.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue growth slow to 21% when two films were released, and what is the digital/non-digital split?
qa_highlights.answer: Songs went live mid-May and June, so full revenue impact was not in Q1; full impact expected from Q2. Digital is around 75% of revenue; no separate split given.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the buyback meeting moved, and what is the size?
qa_highlights.answer: The Board is evaluating an open-market buyback effective August 1 alongside tender offer; decision at the August 5 meeting. Buyback size depends on SEBI and exchange rules; not yet decided.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost recovery status of Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the film's cost should be recovered; satellite and OTT money is still coming and accounting is ongoing, with about 1.5-2 months to complete the cycle.

qa_highlights.question: Any update on YouTube Shorts deal and industry growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: YouTube Shorts still under negotiation, update by end of Q2. Management said industry growth is single digit this year, but Tips is targeting 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise 30% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Labour code changes moved some full-time consultants onto payroll, lowering other expenses; net effect on profit is nil. Q1 run-rate expected to continue.

532375|2026-09.headline: Tips Music Q2 FY27 revenue rose 35% YoY to INR120 crore and EBITDA margin hit 70.5%, with FY27 content spend guided at INR90-100 crore.
532375|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR120 crore, up 35% YoY from INR89.2 crore, with operating EBITDA of INR84.64 crore (70.5% margin, up 25% YoY) and PAT of INR65.5 crore (54% margin, up 23%). H1 FY27 revenue was INR227 crore (up 28%) and H1 PAT INR109 crore (up 11%), with content cost front-loaded at INR71 crore in H1. Management said growth came from both new releases and catalogue, mainly volume-driven, and kept the full-year content guidance at INR90-100 crore. Revenue and PAT growth guidance was stated as 20%, with management saying it would exceed that without giving a specific number. The YouTube Shorts deal remains under negotiation.

532408|2026-09.headline: Sigma Advanced Systems Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 12% QoQ to INR417 crores, with operational EBITDA of INR82.28 crores (19.7% margin).
532408|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached INR417 crores in Q2 FY27, up from INR374 crores in Q1, and operational EBITDA rose to INR82.28 crores from INR61 crores at a 19.7% margin. Profit after tax excluding associate share was INR48.6 crores versus INR35.41 crores in Q1. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,900-2,000 crores at about 20% EBITDA margin, and said the UK operations and Sri City facility are moving work to India to lift margins. Management also announced a planned fundraise of up to INR3,000 crores to fund acquisitions, with closings targeted for Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What has been invested in Nasmyth and Bromford post-acquisition, and what drives margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: About GBP 8-9 million invested across working capital, buffer stock, supply chain and new equipment, lifting OTIF from 65% to about 97%. Insourcing and new kit are expected to continue the quarterly margin improvement over the next couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the purpose and timing of the INR3,000 crore fundraise?
qa_highlights.answer: Primarily to fund acquisitions; management expects transactions to close around Q4, subject to shareholder approval. Management said no working capital raise is needed given cash and working capital lines.

qa_highlights.question: How is the M107 export order accounted for and is the 155mm fuse order a standalone order?
qa_highlights.answer: About 85% of the 40,000-unit M107 order revenue was recognised in Q1 and Q2, with the remaining 15% completing in October and reflecting in Q3. Fuse and shell orders are separate component orders that together form an ammunition solution.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MIL CCF arrangement and time to revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: An exclusive MOU with Munitions India Limited, bringing European partner technology already battle-proven and indigenised in India. Management expects supply to MIL within 6-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the bridge from H1 revenue of about INR800 crores to the INR2,000 crore FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramp-up is expected from aerospace and defence exports, with domestic defence skewed to Q3-Q4. Management cited INR3,915 crores of new orders since July 1, many executing in 12-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: How is the debt position and repayment planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is about INR80 crores, mostly working capital; term loan of INR76 crores with repayment strategy not finalised. Other term borrowings follow a schedule running January 1 to December 31, 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What is the acquisition size and target profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets are businesses with about USD100-150 million revenue, EBITDA positive, with OEM customer access and capacity to transfer work to India. Management said it avoids loss-making companies.

532424|2026-03.headline: GCPL Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 11% in INR on 6% underlying volume growth; EBITDA up 10% at 21.7% margin, with a revenue-presentation change.
532424|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue grew 11% in INR on 6% underlying volume growth, EBITDA grew 10% with a 21.7% margin, and reported PAT grew 10%. India standalone was the standout: 8% volume growth, 10% sales growth, 18% EBITDA growth and a 24.7% margin, led by Home Care (+12%). Africa/US/Middle East grew 20% in sales but EBITDA rose only 2% after doubling media spend, and Indonesia grew 3% in sales with 4% volume growth. From this quarter, customer-related trade spends are netted off revenue following an ICAI Expert Advisory Committee opinion, with no impact on absolute EBITDA or PAT. Management guided to margin pressure in Q1 and likely Q2 FY27 from crude-linked and palm oil input inflation of roughly 7-9%, offset by price hikes and share gains.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said soap markets are muted after GST and a warm/cold weather swing, that Personal Wash gained share, and that pricing will return to soaps, with Personal Care expected to grow faster in FY27 but structurally slower than Home Care.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 21.5% normative margin for India at risk given inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects lower margins for this quarter and next (about 3-4 months of pressure) because crude costs hit all categories, but it expects EBITDA to recover as pricing and share gains come through.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the trade-spend netting on revenue and A&P?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue and the matching other-expense lines fall by the same amount, with no change to EBITDA, PAT or cash flow; A&P looks lower on the new basis but is broadly flat year on year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Fab ARR and path to profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Fab's run-rate is about INR500 crore GSV (about INR450 crore NSV) and it broke even in Q4; the business is now national, with North and Maharashtra growing faster than the South.

qa_highlights.question: How does palm oil inflation compare with the FY22 cycle, and how much pricing is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Palm oil is up about 10-11% (MYR4,000 to 4,500) versus 20-25% in FY22; management said the broader crude-led inflation is spread across categories, making it easier to price than a palm-oil-only spike.

qa_highlights.question: Is the household insecticide problem behind GCPL after RNF?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RNF has worked in most places, HI is shifting from a zero-to-low single-digit category to a high single-digit strategy, and the seasonality issue is improving.

532424|2026-06.headline: GCPL Q1 FY27: consolidated revenue up 19% YoY on 9% underlying volume growth, EBITDA up 14% with 19% margin; India gross margin hit by war-linked input costs.
532424|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 19% YoY with underlying volume growth of 9%, EBITDA rose 14% at a 19% margin, and net profit grew 11%. India gross margin fell sharply as LPG, kerosene and LABSA roughly trebled during the war-driven spike, with India cost impact near 6% over plan. Africa (GAUM) delivered an exceptional quarter with constant-currency growth around 25% and EBITDA margins moving to mid-teens, while Indonesia returned to stable growth at about 10%. Management says it is on track for full-year guidance and expects to exceed it on revenue, and possibly on EBITDA and volume.

segments.name: India Household Insecticides (HI)
segments.commentary: Management says GCPL gained overall HI market share in Q1 FY27 for the first time in almost a decade, driven by incense sticks, not premium segments. June was very weak due to rain and poor fill rates; July first half also poor.

segments.name: India Air care / Speedboats
segments.commentary: Speedboats grew about 3% in Q1 per analyst calculation; salience about 15% and management expects roughly 100-150 bps rise per quarter. Air care in India hit by LPG-linked fill rate falls of 20-25%.

segments.name: Africa / GAUM
segments.commentary: Constant-currency growth about 25%, driven by FMCG (air care at double-digit market share in South Africa within six months of launch) and hair extensions cost improvements. FY26 growth split was about 50:50 FMCG and hair.

segments.name: Indonesia
segments.commentary: Growth about 10% on a slower base, step-up in air media, and early El Nino benefit; Stellar business growing faster.

segments.name: Soaps (India)
segments.commentary: Volumes grew positively in Q1; management expects early single-digit growth in Q2 and Q3, soap margins at normative levels.

segments.name: Muuchstac (acquired DTC brand)
segments.commentary: Growth of about 70-80% from acquisition run rate; EPS accretive from day one, profitable digital-first brand.

segments.name: Pet care
segments.commentary: Committed INR500 crore capital; additional INR200 crore rights commitment referenced by analyst. Product-market fit achieved in Tamil Nadu; expansion to rest of South India under way.

qa_highlights.answer: Management says it is broadly on plan; air fill rates in India fell and salience rises about 100-150 bps per quarter, so full-year targets may be exceeded.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for India volume and pricing trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 India volume 7% is at the lower end; India volume expected to rise about 100 bps a year. Pricing about 5% taken with more possible, but caution as costs fell.

qa_highlights.question: Why did India gross margin fall so sharply and how fast will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: LPG, kerosene and LABSA trebled, with GCPL among the largest LPG and kerosene users in FMCG. Management expects return to normative margins in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is media spend being cut and will it be restored?
qa_highlights.answer: Media spend down about 7-8%, media reach down about 3%; share of voice maintained in core and will be raised as costs ease for new launches.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO Aasif Malbari said the tailwind should last another 4 to 5 months and reduce toward the end of H2.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp Indonesia turnaround?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a slower base, stepped-up air media, El Nino benefit and faster growth in the Stellar business.

532424|2026-09.headline: GCPL Q2 FY27: consolidated revenue up 19% YoY (15% constant currency) on 8% underlying volume growth; net profit up 14% to INR523 crore.
532424|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 19% YoY (15% in constant currency) with 8% underlying volume growth, EBITDA grew 12% and net profit rose 14% to INR523 crore. Standalone sales grew 13% on 7% underlying volume growth, after an estimated 150 bps hit from trade inventory correction, which also mildly hit standalone EBITDA. GUAM (Africa) and Indonesia were the strongest international contributors, while input inflation was among the highest in many years and was offset by pricing, cost savings and A&P optimisation. Management held FY27 guidance of high single-digit standalone UVG and double-digit consolidated revenue and EBITDA growth, and said revenues are running ahead of plan.

financial_highlights.change: Second consecutive quarter of high-teens growth
Management targets double-digit consolidated EBITDA growth in FY27
Underlying volume growth 7%; ~150 bps impact from trade inventory correction
Led by air fresheners and home care liquids

segments.name: Home Care (India)
segments.commentary: Value growth of 19%, led by air fresheners and home care liquids; market share gained in household insecticides (HI). Electric portfolio improved sequentially with the 6 minutes campaign; Godrej Fab grew at a strong double-digit rate.

segments.name: Personal Care (India)
segments.commentary: Value growth of 8%, with soaps stable despite significant price increases and grammage reduction against a favourable comparator. Premium liquids, Cinthol body wash, hair colour (share gains) and perfumes/deodorants (strong double-digit growth) contributed; volume growth lagged value growth.

segments.name: Indonesia
segments.commentary: Sales +20% with 8% underlying volume growth and EBITDA +12%, aided by El Nino-driven mosquito infestation tailwind; LPG prices doubled. Newer portfolio (LV, Pocket) sustained double-digit underlying volume growth.

segments.name: GUAM (Africa)
segments.commentary: Sales +40% INR (+23% constant currency), 16% underlying volume growth, EBITDA +43%; seventh consecutive quarter of double-digit top-line growth and eleventh of double-digit bottom-line growth.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance held: high single-digit underlying volume growth in standalone and double-digit revenue and EBITDA growth at consolidated level; revenues running ahead of plan in H1, with confidence to exceed in certain areas.
Commodity inflation expected to be slightly higher in Q3 than Q2; company will price for profit growth rather than margin, focusing on consolidated EBITDA YoY growth.
Further calibrated pricing planned in soaps and liquid detergents, where margins remain below normative levels.
Management expects to hold double-digit consolidated EBITDA growth; India EBITDA shape expected to broadly continue with some up-and-down quarters.
International business expected to deliver double-digit volume growth; Indonesia growth at higher levels still to be proven.
Capacity expansions for GUAM businesses at high utilisation due in the next few months.
capex_capacity: GUAM existing businesses running at very high capacity utilisation, constraining growth; capacity expansions due in the next few months.
Godrej Spic (toilet cleaner) scaled nationally after Tamil Nadu success; significant distribution headroom remains.
Trade inventory being reduced to system-defined levels to support primary sales run without manual intervention.
demand_pricing: Input costs: one of the highest inflationary impacts in many years, driven by crude derivatives, palm oil and commodities; impact approximately high single digit in India and Indonesia.
Pricing actions taken across portfolio, large cost-savings programme, and media/trade spend optimisation used to offset inflation; share of voice to be kept range-bound.
Soaps category seeing trade inventory correction, price-volume recalibration and grammage cuts; detergents growth described as strong, with powder-to-liquid shift and formalisation benefit.

Media spend in India standalone declined for seven consecutive quarters (per analyst: -7% in Q1, -17% in Q2); management attributes it equally to category spend reduction in soaps/detergents and to better-reach, lower-cost media buying in the rest of the portfolio.
New launches: Godrej Rizz (selected West and South India markets), Godrej Zap stain remover online, GUAM HI incense sticks; Ezee entering season with early traction.

qa_highlights.question: What changed in digital advertising capability, daily sales hustle, and HI communication since the management transition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said digital and influencer capabilities are being built and it expects top-percentile digital positioning within a few quarters, not tied to spend percentage. Operational excellence focus is being reset via trade inventory correction. New HI ad features the RNF product and is designed to be clutter-breaking.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline and skill-set for the India CEO hire, and progress on pet care and new bathroom cleaner?
qa_highlights.answer: India CEO search is in a robust process, prioritising Godrej values and entrepreneurial mindset over speed. Godrej Spic is now national. Pet care is still in learning phase; management will give milestones next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Personal Care volume growth well below 8% value growth, and which parts are weak?
qa_highlights.answer: Soaps saw trade inventory correction (large SKUs typically build inventory) and price-volume recalibration after steep price increases; margins still below normative. Hair colour gained share strongly. Detergents growth is in line with trend.

qa_highlights.question: How should Q3/Q4 India margins and EBITDA be viewed given commodity lag?
qa_highlights.answer: Commodity inflation expected slightly higher in Q3 vs Q2. Company will focus on consolidated EBITDA YoY growth rather than margin, aiming to hold double-digit consolidated EBITDA growth; India may see some up-and-down quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Are H2 volume risks from inflation or season in detergents and HI?
qa_highlights.answer: Detergents not impacted by inflation on volume; HI season looks fine as El Nino impact was mainly in H1. Management expects to sustain volume trend lines.

qa_highlights.question: Is the decline in India standalone A&P spend structural or cyclical?
qa_highlights.answer: Both: soaps and detergents category spend has fallen and the company is balancing spend to keep share of voice at target, while the rest of the portfolio gets higher reach at lower cost via media agency practices. Management gave roughly equal weight to the two factors.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are Indonesia and GUAM growth beyond this year, and what is GUAM's mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Indonesia: a few bps of this year's growth is attributed to better weather; management is building more growth flywheels and expects double-digit international volume growth. GUAM: growth is broad-based, from core hair and new categories like Mega Growth Mousse and Darling styling products; hair colour has grown double digit in volume for 7-8 quarters. No split of core vs new given.

risks_watch: Trade inventory correction in soaps and large SKUs may continue to weigh on standalone sales and EBITDA.
Commodity inflation expected to be higher in Q3 than Q2; pricing actions need to offset without hurting volumes, especially in soaps.
Indonesia's growth benefited from El Nino-driven weather; management acknowledged this is partly seasonal.
India CEO appointment still pending; management transition and team changes (digital, operational excellence) are still being put in place.
A&P spend in India standalone has declined for seven consecutive quarters; watch share of voice and brand investment.
Pet care business still in pilot with no milestones disclosed until next quarter.

532439|2026-09.headline: Olectra Q2 FY27 revenue rose only 4.6% to ₹687 crore, though H1 revenue grew 25.8% to ₹1,262.5 crore and EBITDA margin recovered to 16%.
532439|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was ₹687 crore, up 4.6% YoY, while Q2 EBITDA rose 18.2% to ₹109.9 crore with margin up to 16% from 14.2%. H1 revenue grew 25.8% to ₹1,262.5 crore and H1 EBITDA rose 22.7% to ₹182.8 crore, but margin eased to 14.5% from 14.8%. Mobility drove results: Q2 mobility segment profit rose 18.1%, and the company delivered a record 401 vehicles in the quarter, though mix shifted toward lower-priced 9-metre buses. Energy segment profit fell in Q2 and H1 despite strong revenue growth, as export mix and margins normalised.

financial_highlights.change: +30.1% YoY vs ₹81.7 crore; ~72% of H1 segment profit
vs cash outflow in prior year

segments.name: Mobility (electric buses)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue broadly flat YoY while H1 revenue rose about 24.7%; record 401 deliveries in Q2 and 749 in H1 vs 536 a year ago. Q2 revenue was held back by mix, with most deliveries 9-metre buses (~₹1.1 crore each vs ~₹1.45 crore for 12-metre). Management says mobility margins are back at about 14%.

segments.name: Energy (polymer/composite insulators)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 30% in Q2 and 37.2% in H1, but segment profit fell 6.5% in Q2 and 4.5% in H1 on lower exports and higher raw material and environmental costs. Export share was about 13% in H1 vs about 40% a year earlier; management guides to a 25-30% margin range, down from about 35% last year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects to keep growing at 20-25%, in line with the first half.
Management is cautiously optimistic on FY27 growth and aims for sustainable, profitable growth while managing working capital and finance costs.
Energy segment margin target of 25-30%, with export mix expected to recover by one to two points.

Olectra claims ~22%+ market share in e-buses, in the top two among about 14 players; about 13 players in e-trucks.

Private bus demand: Fresh Bus has run five to six lakh km on the company's initial batch of buses.

qa_highlights.question: Why did energy segment margin fall from about 35% to about 25%, and how does it compare with a peer reporting around 40%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it could not verify peer data and industry margins are about 25-30%. It said 35% was a peak year helped by strong export demand. It now targets a stable 25-30% range, with H1 export share at about 13% vs about 40% last year due to US trade-duty changes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue barely rise in mobility despite volumes up about 7%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to mix: most Q2 deliveries were 9-metre buses at a lower price point. Mix will vary with contract timing. Order book is mixed, with 9-metre below 50%, and 12-metre volume share is expected to rise.

qa_highlights.question: Is Olectra losing ground in e-trucks to new entrants, and what about the expansion plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Olectra is in the top two in e-buses with ~22% share and plans to lead in trucks. It is building a prototype, with launch at end-Q4 or early Q1 FY28, and is relying on its ~750 million km of bus operating experience and 117 trucks in the market. No specific expansion details were given.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the Tamil Nadu 12-metre AC e-bus tender and private bus opportunities?
qa_highlights.answer: The tender is under technical evaluation, bid through an operating partner, with outcome expected this month. Engagement with Fresh Bus and other private operators continues, and a 13.5-metre bus is in development.

qa_highlights.question: Will the composite insulator business be demerged, and what is the status of GFRP rebar and related litigation?
qa_highlights.answer: No demerger proposal exists yet; the board will consider it and disclose after approval. The GFRP rebar business was prototyped but dropped on margin concerns. Management said there is no litigation on the matter raised by the questioner.

Tamil Nadu tender outcome due this month; e-truck launch timing and competition from new entrants.

532440|2026-03.headline: MPS FY26 revenue rose 5.7% to INR 768 crore and EBITDA 11.8% to INR 236 crore; FY27 EBITDA guided to comfortably exceed INR 300 crore.
532440|2026-03.overview: FY26 was described as the most profitable year in company history, with EBITDA margin at 30.7% and PAT up 16.3% to INR 173 crore. Q4 revenue grew 12.7% to INR 205 crore and EBITDA margin expanded to 32.9%, helped by Research and the Unbound Medicine acquisition, which closed on 9 February 2026. Corporate Learning revenue fell 16.5% for the year but returned to positive year-on-year growth in Q4. Management guided FY27 EBITDA above INR 300 crore on an organic, bottom-up basis, and no final dividend was recommended for FY26 because capital was deployed into Unbound and the M&A pipeline.

financial_highlights.value: INR 113.75 crore; borrowings INR 40.25 crore (Unbound facility)

segments.name: Research Solutions
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 464 crore, EBITDA margin 39.9% (+330 bps); organic growth 17% ex-AJE. Q4 revenue INR 120 crore (+7.6% YoY), EBITDA INR 50 crore at 41.6% margin; organic core grew 23% YoY in Q4.

segments.name: Education Solutions
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 209 crore, organic growth 28.6%; EBITDA INR 82 crore at 39.2% margin, up 42.6% reported. Q4 revenue INR 60 crore (+30.5% YoY). Unbound contributed INR 11.78 crore over 50 days, about 19.6% of Q4 Education revenue.

segments.name: Corporate Learning (Liberate Global)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 96 crore, down 16.5% YoY; headcount down about 32% YoY. Q4 revenue INR 25.5 crore (+2.4% YoY, first positive print of year); Q4 EBITDA INR 6.7 crore at 26.3% margin, up 55% QoQ.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA to comfortably cross INR 300 crore, built bottom-up from segment plans; implies about 21% EBITDA CAGR FY24-FY27 and excludes any acquisitions beyond Unbound.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected in the 30%-35% range, with margins typically expanding as revenue grows.
Indicative FY27 split of EBITDA: Research about 55%, Education about 35%, Corporate Learning about 10% (management said it was ballpark only).

Unbound Medicine: FY27 monthly revenue expected at USD 750,000-950,000 (seasonal), starting at about 15% EBITDA margin and exiting at 25%-30%; historical run rate USD 700,000-800,000 per month at 18%-19% margin.
FY28 target of about INR 1,500 crore revenue (Vision 2027) reaffirmed as intact; tighter FY28 guidance to be given at end of Q3 or Q4 FY27.
No final dividend for FY26; management said distributions resume when the current deployment cycle closes.

MPS Labs is a 200-engineer AI R&D team; Think365 platform in live production after about 2 years of build.
Research Integrity Check (RIC) and DigiCore Pro scaling across renewal cohort; JEO office (pre-acceptance) identified as the highest-margin Research line.
Corporate Learning shifting to AI, AR/VR and simulation-led builds; Bridge AI multilingual translation in active enterprise deployment.
demand_pricing: Research: pre-acceptance (B2B) services grew more than 90%; AJE pruning described as complete. AJE growth drivers are premium author tiers, AI-driven productivity, and cross-selling to corporate publishers.

Education: AI-accessibility line (more than 30 million auto-generated accessible media assets a year) roughly tripled revenue in FY26.
Corporate Learning: Q4 order book the strongest of FY26; new entrants added at top customer relationships.
Management argued AI commoditises basic production work and raises demand for trusted, verified AI in high-stakes knowledge workflows; company's share of serviceable market is about 0.5%.

qa_highlights.question: What is MPS's right to win in a market where it holds only about 0.5% share, and what capabilities are needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited an AI-first knowledge positioning in high-stakes layers, an integrated platform stack (HighWire, Think365, RIC, Bridge AI, Unbound, DigiCore), 200+ MPS Labs engineers, and deep expansion within large accounts. The target path is 0.5% to 1% to 2% over several years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 1,500 crore FY28 revenue target still achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is intact and in line of sight. FY27 INR 300 crore EBITDA is organic and excludes new acquisitions; any further M&A would sit on top. Tighter FY28 guidance to come at end-Q3 or Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Are there more acquisitions, and has Unbound been paid for?
qa_highlights.answer: Unbound is mostly fully paid, with only small closing amounts left. Pipeline is active, with a Western Higher Ed carve-out the most advanced. Management will disclose material deals in the ordinary course.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 EBITDA margin expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a margin in the 30%-35% range, with expansion as revenue grows.

qa_highlights.question: What is Unbound's revenue and EBITDA, and how will it move in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: The 50-day consolidation gave INR 11-12 crore revenue at 18.5%-19% margin. Monthly run rate was USD 700,000-800,000. FY27 expected USD 750,000-950,000 per month, starting near 15% EBITDA margin and exiting at 25%-30%.

qa_highlights.question: Given AI disruption, what protects the business model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI compresses commoditised production work but raises demand for trusted AI in medicine, scholarly publishing and regulated learning. It sees agentic AI as a tailwind, with verification as the gating constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margin dip and ex-AJE headcount rise, and what drives FY27 growth and the FY28 path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AJE headcount moved offshore to India while Research headcount rose ahead of expected growth, causing a timing-related ex-AJE margin softness in Q4. Growth drivers are the four Research product layers, Education, and the accessibility line.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Corporate Learning investment shift, and why did clients rise while revenue per client fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Work has moved from compliance content to AI, AR/VR and simulation-led performance enablers. Unbound added a long tail of smaller institutional accounts, which lowered average revenue per client without any anchor client billing less.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA split and main risk to the INR 300 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave a ballpark split of Research 55%, Education 35%, Corporate 10%. It sees no company-specific risk, only broader geopolitical and macro risk. Management disputed the analyst's constant-currency framing.

qa_highlights.question: What are the non-Unbound niche criteria for future acquisitions?

532443|2026-03.headline: Cera Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11.4% YoY to INR 644 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 15.2% from 18.3% on brass costs and trade discounts.

EBITDA excluding other income fell to INR 98 crore (15.2% margin) from INR 106 crore (18.3%), driven by brass input costs, elevated trade discounts and pre-operating costs for Senator and Polipluz. Price increases were taken in March (11% effective) and April-May (surcharge then 8% sanitaryware and 5% faucetware), with management targeting a 14-15% EBITDA margin. Morbi gas disruptions were cited as an opportunity, with Cera running inventory and internalising outsourced SKUs. FY26 revenue was INR 2,050 crore, and FY27 guidance is 18-20% growth.

532454|2026-03.headline: Airtel FY26 consolidated revenue hit a record ~Rs 2,11,000 Cr; Q4 India ARPU rose only Rs 3 to Rs 257 on EDB basis.
